title: Strive Raises $630M in SATS Nasdaq Debut With 15% Dividend Tied to Bitcoin Strategy
summary:
Key Takeaways: Strive successfully closed an IPO of an upsized $630 million, in its perpetual preferred stock. SATS pays 1.5% compounded on a $100 stated value, payable on each business
The post Strive Raises $630M in SATS Nasdaq Debut With 15% Dividend Tied to Bitcoin Strategy appeared first on Cry...
content:
Key Takeaways:

  • Strive successfully closed an IPO of an upsized $630 million, in its perpetual preferred stock.
  • SATS pays 1.5% compounded on a $100 stated value, payable on each business day.
  • Strive received new funds from the offering which could go towards future Bitcoin investments; the specific amount of Bitcoin was not specified.

Strive has gone one step further in the public markets with its Nasdaq listing of SATS, a new perpetual preferred security on the basis of fixed income and corporate stakes in Bitcoin. The company sold a total of 7 million shares of SATS at $90 a share, grossing $630 million.

  • Strive’s SATS IPO Brings in $630 Million
  • Daily Dividends Add a Different Structure to Bitcoin Exposure
    • Bitcoin Purchases Remain a Major Possibility
    • SATS Expands Strive’s Bitcoin-Focused Capital Stack

Strive’s SATS IPO Brings in $630 Million

Strive announced the closing of the upsized offering on October 20, with SATS expected to trade on the Nasdaq Global Market under the ticker SATS.

SATS is now listed on Nasdaq.

15.00% fixed annualized dividend rate based on $100 stated amount. Paid every business day.

First dividend: November 9, 2026, inclusive of dividends accrued since the October 20 closing.

$SATS $ASST $SATA https://t.co/uHFnzEW9LN

— Strive (@Strive) October 20, 2026

The preferred shares have a sum of $100 and carry a cumulative dividend at 15% per annum. This annual amount is $15 per share when dividends are declared and fully paid. This is the nominal annual dividend, which corresponds to about 16.7% of the price of the Offering.

Dividend payments will happen every day a business is in operation from November 9, 2026. If the payment is declared in full, it will cover dividends from October 20 when declared.

Read More: Bitwise Launches First U.S. Spot NEAR ETF With 5% Staking Rewards and $32B Intents

Daily Dividends Add a Different Structure to Bitcoin Exposure

SATS is a perpetual product: that is, there is no traditional date of maturity. Strive is pitching the security as a cash flow tool in addition to another favored choice in the capital structure, SATA. For the company, SATS is an additional measure to boost its “Amplification Ratio”, which the firm believes is at the heart of its ability to benchmark better than Bitcoin over time, CEO Matt Cole said.

In addition, Chief Risk Officer Jeff Walton highlighted that Strive has no debt or impending debt due and has no other fixed financial obligations apart from dividends at this time.

Bitcoin Purchases Remain a Major Possibility

Strive has not locked up all of the offering into Bitcoin. The funds received can be applied to general corporate uses, such as Bitcoin purchases, cash flow of working capital, income-producing assets, expenditures on capital, acquisitions, repurchasing shares as disclosed in company notes to regulatory submissions.

With that being said, unknowns remain about who the last Bitcoinmaker will be. The offering, according to outside estimates, is expected to net around $608 million, excluding underwriting expenses and other costs. If all that was invested in Bitcoin, it represents the purchase of more than 7,300 BTC at a representative price of close to $82,500.

Strive has also stated it currently holds 36,818 BTC, which would result in its capital above 44,000 BTC if it fully allocated every BTC stored.

SATS Expands Strive’s Bitcoin-Focused Capital Stack

Since the listing, Strive has obtained a further capital raising mechanism, apart from by way of traditional debt. While Strive continues to go the Bitcoin route on its balance sheet, the main thrust of focus of SATS is predictable income.

The company described the preferred stock as part of a broader family of liquid financial securities aimed at investors seeking different combinations of income, price stability and Bitcoin-linked corporate exposure.

Read More: StablecoinX’s $275M ENA Treasury Sends USDE to Nasdaq in Historic Stablecoin Debut

title: Project Eleven and Relm Explore Quantum Risks in Crypto Insurance
summary: Project Eleven has partnered with Bermuda-based Relm Insurance to explore incorporating post-quantum security controls into digital asset insurance underwriting. Assessing Post-Quantum Risk Models Post-quantum security firm Project Eleven announced a development partnership on Tuesday with Relm Insu...
content:
Project Eleven has partnered with Bermuda-based Relm Insurance to explore incorporating post-quantum security controls into digital asset insurance underwriting.

Key Takeaways

  • Project Eleven has partnered with Relm Insurance to assess post-quantum risks.
  • Strongpoint helps institutional digital asset holders update cryptography without losing audit history.
  • Relm will explore post-quantum controls to shape future underwriting frameworks for Web3 clients.

Assessing Post-Quantum Risk Models

Post-quantum security firm Project Eleven announced a development partnership on Tuesday with Relm Insurance to explore how quantum computing threats can be evaluated within digital asset insurance underwriting.

The collaboration centers on Project Eleven’s flagship institutional custody platform, Strongpoint. Built to address emerging quantum computing risks, Strongpoint combines classical and post-quantum signing methods, allowing financial institutions to upgrade cryptographic algorithms without disrupting existing approval workflows or audit records.

As quantum computing technology progresses, experts warn that a powerful enough quantum computer could derive private keys from exposed public keys, exposing digital assets to theft or compromise.

Under the partnership, Relm and Project Eleven will examine how post-quantum security controls can be integrated into digital asset risk models. Relm will also advise on Strongpoint’s design to ensure custody infrastructure provides the necessary auditability and risk evidence required by underwriters.

“Every institution holding digital assets will eventually need to prepare for post-quantum cryptography. The open question is whether that transition happens on the institution’s schedule or under pressure,” said Alex Pruden, CEO and co-founder of Project Eleven. “Insurance plays a critical role in how markets assess and manage risk. We believe there is an opportunity for institutions that invest in stronger post-quantum defenses to eventually see that reflected in how their risk is evaluated.”

Evolving Risk Landscape in Digital Assets

Joseph Ziolkowski, founder and CEO of Relm Insurance, emphasized the necessity of anticipating technological shifts in underwriting.

“Insuring exposures across the digital asset ecosystem requires underwriters to anticipate how risks will evolve,” Ziolkowski said. “Quantum computing is a clear example of an emerging threat that should shape the way we assess risk today. Our work with Project Eleven will explore how institutions identify their exposure, demonstrate effective controls, and prepare for the transition to post-quantum readiness.”

The companies noted that the partnership is currently exploratory. Any potential impact on insurance underwriting criteria or premium rates will depend on further evaluation and Relm’s independent underwriting procedures.

The initiative comes as specialty insurers expand risk coverage for emerging and high-risk sectors. Relm Insurance, a Bermuda-based insurer specializing in digital assets and cannabis, launched a specialized kidnap and ransom insurance product tailored for Web3 and crypto executives.

The move was prompted by a surge in physical threats, extortion, and targeted attacks against high-profile digital asset founders and executives, whose public exposure often makes them targets for ransom and extortion schemes. By pairing traditional risk coverage with post-quantum defense evaluations, Relm is expanding its focus on both physical and technical threat mitigation across the digital asset sector.

title: Musk says SpaceX-Tesla merger a ‘good idea’ as AI revenue jumps ninefold
summary: A merger would bring Tesla into the same corporate group as Grok developer SpaceXAI and social media platform X.
content:
Elon Musk said he likes the idea of merging Tesla with SpaceX in a potential move that would create a roughly $3.5 trillion technology giant combining AI, space exploration and electric vehicle manufacturing. 

“Do I think it would be a good idea? Yes,” Musk said of the potential merger during a SpaceX Q3 earnings call on Tuesday.

Musk said that both SpaceX and Tesla have formed special committees of independent directors to discuss the idea at the request of shareholders, though he isn’t able to take part in the discussions due to being a conflicted party.

A merger would bring Tesla into the same corporate group as Grok developer SpaceXAI (formerly xAI) and social media platform X, which SpaceX acquired in February. The talks also come as SpaceX’s AI business became its largest revenue segment in Q3, underscoring how central artificial intelligence has become to Musk’s expanding technology empire.

“There’s a lot to be gained from cooperating on developing superintelligence software, chip design, the Terafab, obviously, robotics, mass to orbit with the Starmind constellation. Connectivity,” said Musk.  

However, Musk tempered expectations of whether a merger will ultimately come through.

“Some people out there assume that a SpaceX and Tesla merger is a certainty, and I think that would be overstating it,” he said, adding that the special committees have not reached agreement on terms of any transaction and there is no guarantee that they will.

“At the end of the day, the shareholders have to be supportive of this and particularly on Tesla’s side we’ll need a 50% vote of all shares, not just those who vote, but of all shareholders. And that’s quite a high hurdle to try to achieve.”

SpaceX Q3 earnings show huge AI revenue gains

Musk’s comments followed SpaceX’s third-quarter earnings report, which showed revenue rising 161% year over year to $14.6 billion, driven largely by its “Super Intelligence” AI segment. 

SpaceX’s Super Intelligence segment generated $7.6 billion in third-quarter revenue, an 830% increase from a year earlier, making it the company’s largest revenue contributor. 

Related: Crypto Biz: SpaceX fuels tokenization’s next boom

SpaceX said the growth was driven by the activation of new cloud services agreements, the acquisition of Cursor and increased adoption of its agentic AI model Grok across enterprise and consumers. 

Combined Bitcoin holdings would exceed 30,000 BTC

A Tesla–SpaceX merger could also bring two sizable corporate Bitcoin treasuries under one roof. SpaceX reported holding 18,712 Bitcoin as of June 30, while Tesla held 11,509 BTC on the same date, according to their respective quarterly filings. 

Based on those disclosures, a combined company would hold 30,221 BTC, which would make it the sixth-largest public Bitcoin treasury company, beating crypto exchange Bullish.

title: Musk’s SpaceX Earnings Rocket Higher as Bitcoin Stash Holds Firm
summary: SpaceX delivered a blockbuster third quarter, generating $14.6 billion in revenue, $4.4 billion in net income, and $8.8 billion in adjusted EBITDA. Behind those extraordinary earnings, Elon Musk’s company reported $1.573 billion in digital assets, consistent with its previously disclosed bitcoin hol...
content:
SpaceX delivered a blockbuster third quarter, generating $14.6 billion in revenue, $4.4 billion in net income, and $8.8 billion in adjusted EBITDA. Behind those extraordinary earnings, Elon Musk’s company reported $1.573 billion in digital assets, consistent with its previously disclosed bitcoin holdings of 18,712 BTC. Artificial intelligence (AI) now leads the company’s revenue machine, while Musk’s personal fortune has reportedly climbed to $925 billion.

Key Takeaways

  • SpaceX generated $14.6 billion in third-quarter revenue, a 161% increase year over year.
  • SpaceX reported $1.573 billion in digital assets, consistent with its previously disclosed 18,712 BTC.
  • Forbes valued Elon Musk’s fortune at approximately $925 billion on Oct. 20, 2026.

SpaceX’s AI Empire Delivers Record Growth While Bitcoin Stash Holds Firm

SpaceX came out swinging Tuesday, Oct. 20, delivering third-quarter earnings that left Wall Street’s expectations in the dust. Revenue climbed 161% to $14.6 billion, while the aerospace and AI powerhouse transformed a $1.1 billion year-earlier loss into $4.4 billion in profit.

But buried deeper in the financial statements was another billion-dollar figure worth examining: $1.573 billion in digital assets, consistent with the company’s longstanding bitcoin treasury. For Elon Musk, whose business empire now stretches from orbital launches to AI, the latest earnings demonstrate how thoroughly SpaceX has evolved beyond its rocket-building origins.

SpaceX Earnings Crush Expectations as AI Becomes the Main Attraction

The newly publicly traded company, SpaceX reported $2.8 billion in operating income and $8.8 billion in adjusted earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization (EBITDA), representing a 306% year-over-year increase. Diluted earnings reached 35 cents per share, comfortably ahead of estimates ranging from approximately 13 to 16 cents, while revenue surpassed forecasts of $12.7 billion to $12.9 billion.

The real showstopper was SpaceX’s Super Intelligence division, which raked in $7.56 billion, an astonishing 830% increase from the previous year. The business, encompassing Grok, cloud infrastructure and the recently acquired Cursor operation, overtook Starlink as SpaceX’s largest revenue contributor. Operating income reached $431 million, reversing a $1.72 billion loss during the comparable quarter in 2025.

Starlink wasn’t exactly sitting idle. The connectivity division generated $5.25 billion in revenue, up 69%, supported by 13.6 million consumer subscribers. Traditional space operations contributed another $1.77 billion, while the company’s first revenue-generating Starship mission successfully deployed 26 next-generation Starlink satellites.

SpaceX’s 18,712 Bitcoin Remain a Billion-Dollar Fixture

Tucked into page 10 of SpaceX’s earnings report, the consolidated balance sheet lists $1.573 billion under “Digital assets” as of Sept. 30, 2026. That compares with $1.637 billion at the end of December 2025, reflecting a $64 million decline in reported value.

Although the quarterly earnings release doesn’t explicitly identify bitcoin or disclose the number of coins held, previous filings established SpaceX’s position at 18,712 BTC, acquired at an approximate $661 million cost basis. Blockchain intelligence platform Arkham Intelligence also tracks the company’s holdings at 18,712 BTC, primarily associated with Coinbase Prime custody.

The distinction matters. The $64 million reduction in reported digital asset value does not necessarily represent a sale. In fact, SpaceX’s cash flow statement records a corresponding $64 million unrealized loss on digital assets during the first nine months of 2026, consistent with changes in market valuation rather than a confirmed disposal.

For a company increasingly dominated by artificial intelligence, bitcoin remains a sizable, if comparatively quiet, financial holding. The latest earnings materials provide no indication of additional purchases or sales, leaving the previously disclosed treasury position intact based on available information.

Musk’s $925 Billion Fortune Inches Toward Trillionaire Territory

SpaceX’s extraordinary growth isn’t coming cheaply. Capital expenditures totaled $19.6 billion during the quarter, with $16.4 billion directed toward its Super Intelligence division. Nevertheless, the company finished September holding approximately $89.9 billion in cash and marketable securities, providing considerable financial ammunition for its ambitious expansion plans.

Meanwhile, Musk continues to occupy the summit of the global wealth rankings. Forbes’ Real-Time Billionaires list valued his fortune at approximately $925 billion on Oct. 20, 2026, reflecting a $1.4 billion increase from the previous trading day.

Much of that wealth remains tied to his ownership stakes in SpaceX and Tesla, meaning the figure can shift dramatically with market valuations. Still, with SpaceX posting multibillion-dollar profits, an expanding AI empire and a bitcoin treasury worth more than $1.5 billion, Musk now finds himself within striking distance of something once confined to financial fiction: a personal fortune approaching $1 trillion.

title: The Trades Your Algorithm Rejects May Be the Most  Important Data You Never Measure
summary:
Most trading systems are very good at remembering what they bought.
They record entry prices, exits, profits, losses, holding periods and dozens of other variables.
When a trade succeeds, analysts can study why. When it fails, they can study that too.
But there is another group of decisions that ...
content:
Skip to content

Most trading systems are very good at remembering what they bought. They record entry prices, exits, profits, losses, holding periods and dozens of other variables. When a trade succeeds, analysts can study why. When it fails, they can study that too. But there is another group of decisions that often disappears almost completely: the trades the system rejected.

That creates an important blind spot.

Imagine an automated crypto trading system evaluates 1,000 possible opportunities and rejects 950 of them. It executes only 50 trades.

The developer can carefully analyse the performance of those 50 trades. But that still does not answer a basic question:

Were the other 950 rejections good decisions?

A filter may appear to protect a trading system because the trades it accepts perform reasonably well. But without observing what happened after rejection, nobody can know how many losses the filter successfully avoided or how many potentially profitable opportunities it discarded.

This problem became increasingly important to me while studying algorithmic decision-making on decentralised exchanges.

Rejection is also a decision

A trading system does not make decisions only when it buys or sells.

Choosing not to trade is also a decision.

Suppose a token is rejected because its liquidity is too low. Another is rejected because of wallet concentration. A third fails a momentum threshold.

Twenty-four hours later, the first token collapses, the second becomes inactive and the third rises sharply.

Those outcomes contain information about the filters that made the original decisions.

But if the system stopped observing each token at the moment it rejected it, that information has been lost.

This creates an asymmetry in the data.

Accepted decisions naturally generate histories because capital is attached to them. Rejected decisions can disappear from the record even though they may greatly outnumber accepted ones.

I wanted to measure that missing side of the decision process.

Following what the algorithm rejected

I developed Post-Rejection Follow-up Sampling, or PRFS, as a framework for doing this systematically.

The basic idea is simple.

When an algorithm rejects a candidate, do not throw the candidate away.

Record the decision and continue observing the asset.

The process can preserve the time of rejection, the reason for rejection, the market conditions visible at that moment and subsequent observations at predefined intervals.

The order matters.

The decision comes first. The subsequent market path is observed afterward.

In my PRFS audit, the dataset contained approximately 67,000 forward observations associated with 2,997 rejection events involving 457 unique token mints.

The audit also exposed another important lesson.

Collecting more data does not automatically solve a measurement problem.

The identity of the decision being followed, the timing of observations and the way those observations are connected back to the original rejection all matter.

A large dataset can still answer the wrong question if those relationships are incorrectly recorded.

Making rejected decisions measurable

I also developed RED-2400, a public benchmark designed around algorithmically rejected trading events.

The objective was not to produce another trading strategy or claim that one filter could predict token prices.

It was to make the rejected side of the decision process observable.

Once that information exists, researchers can ask much better questions.

Did a particular filter mostly reject assets that subsequently deteriorated?

Did it repeatedly discard assets that later appreciated?

Did its effectiveness change under different market conditions?

Are several filters rejecting essentially the same population for different reasons?

And perhaps most importantly:

Is a trading system being improved based only on the small fraction of opportunities that the system itself made observable?

Independent developers are beginning to test the idea

One of the most encouraging developments has occurred outside my own research.

Independent developers have since built rejection follow-up ledgers and related post-rejection tracking into their own systems.

Some have created persistent ledgers for rejected signals rather than allowing those decisions to disappear from process memory. Others have implemented post-rejection trackers that continue observing rejected candidates at predefined intervals so that screening rules can later be evaluated against what actually happened.

Other independent researchers have used public data from my work to investigate selection and survivorship bias in their own trading datasets and strategy experiments.

This matters to me because research becomes much more informative when someone other than its author tries to use it.

An external implementation can expose limitations, reveal new applications and sometimes show that an apparently promising strategy should not be deployed at all.

That last outcome deserves more attention.

Sometimes the valuable result is deciding not to trade

Financial research is often presented as valuable when it discovers something profitable.

But identifying something that should not be deployed can also have economic value.

Suppose a strategy looks profitable in historical data.

A broader dataset then reveals that successful assets were disproportionately represented in the original sample. Or a more realistic replay shows that the apparent advantage disappears after transaction costs.

The useful result is no longer a profitable backtest.

The useful result is avoiding a potentially bad decision.

This is especially important in fast-moving crypto markets, where small samples, changing liquidity and selection effects can produce attractive historical results that may not survive real-world conditions.

A system capable of discovering evidence against its own decisions may ultimately be more useful than one designed only to find apparent winners.

This problem extends beyond crypto

Reject-side measurement is not only a cryptocurrency problem.

Consider credit underwriting.

A lender naturally observes repayment performance for approved borrowers. The outcomes of rejected applicants are much harder to observe under the same lending decision.

Consider fraud detection.

Cases that pass through later stages of investigation may generate rich labels, while cases removed earlier in the pipeline can receive much less follow-up.

Similar problems can appear in insurance, risk screening, recommendation systems and other machine-learning applications.

The details differ, but the underlying problem is related.

Automated systems increasingly filter large populations before taking action on a much smaller subset.

If researchers evaluate only the population that survives those filters, they may end up evaluating a population partly created by the system itself.

Build systems that remember their “no”

As financial systems become more automated, I believe their audit trails should preserve more than executed actions.

Rejected decisions should become first-class data.

What did the system see?

Why did it say no?

What happened afterward?

Was the rejection ultimately consistent with the system’s objective?

And does the same rule continue to behave similarly when market conditions change?

These questions become even more important as financial decision-making moves toward machine-learning models and increasingly autonomous agents.

A trading algorithm that records only its trades remembers what it did.

A system that also follows its rejections can begin to measure whether its decisions were actually useful.

The data currently discarded may contain some of the most important information about whether automated financial systems deserve confidence.

This article is for information only and is not investment advice.

Research links

Post-Rejection Follow-up Sampling (PRFS): arXiv:2606.08228

RED-2400: arXiv:2605.12151

About the author

Arati Uday Kamat is an independent researcher working on algorithmic decentralised-exchange trading, reject-side outcome measurement and financial-system evaluation. Her research includes Post-Rejection Follow-up Sampling (PRFS), arXiv:2606.08228, and RED-2400, arXiv:2605.12151, a public benchmark for studying rejected trading decisions.

title: Crypto Thieves Hijack Ngrave Alerts and Walk Away With $2.56M
summary: A fake security warning flashed across crypto wallets, sending users scrambling to protect their funds. Instead, the alert delivered them straight to thieves who drained roughly $2.56 million, exploiting a trusted notification system without ever cracking the hardware itself. A Fake Security Alert W...
content:
A fake security warning flashed across crypto wallets, sending users scrambling to protect their funds. Instead, the alert delivered them straight to thieves who drained roughly $2.56 million, exploiting a trusted notification system without ever cracking the hardware itself.

Key Takeaways

  • Ngrave traced approximately $2.56 million stolen from 70 wallet addresses across four blockchain networks.
  • Ngrave said its ZERO hardware remained secure while phishing victims surrendered wallet recovery credentials.
  • Ngrave’s CEO admitted the company had “absolutely and utterly failed” its fundamental security obligation.

A Fake Security Alert With a $2.56 Million Price Tag

Belgian hardware-wallet maker Ngrave, commonly known as NGRAVE, disclosed on Oct. 19 that attackers hijacked a third-party notification provider serving its LIQUID companion app. The breach allowed criminals to send authentic-looking security warnings directly to customers on Oct. 17. The message claimed a user’s portfolio had been synchronized with a Pixel 9 device in Moscow. Clicking the alert opened a counterfeit Ngrave website featuring a countdown timer and an ominous choice to approve or deny the suspicious activity.

Both paths led to the same trap. Users were prompted to enter their 24-word recovery phrase or Perfect Key, handing attackers everything needed to recreate their wallets. Automated scripts emptied compromised accounts within minutes. Ngrave’s investigation traced approximately $2.56 million stolen from 70 wallet addresses across four networks. Bitcoin accounted for $1.77 million, followed by $454,000 in XRP, $316,000 in Ethereum-based assets and $18,000 in Stellar.

Attackers Exploited Notification Keys, Not Hardware

The company’s incident report reveals that unauthorized access potentially began Oct. 11, six days before the fraudulent notifications appeared. Attackers obtained one access key and leveraged it to acquire another with broader permissions, including access to certain analytics information. Ngrave detected the malicious alerts within a minute of their appearance at 9:30 p.m. UTC on Oct. 17. Nevertheless, the first wallet was drained six minutes later.

The company disabled its notification system by 10:45 p.m., but thefts continued from previously compromised wallets until 3:51 a.m. the following morning. Crucially, Ngrave maintains its ZERO hardware wallets and private keys remained untouched. The criminals instead manipulated customers into surrendering their own credentials.

Ngrave CEO Admits Company ‘Absolutely and Utterly Failed’

The stolen funds traveled through exchanges, blockchain bridges, and fresh addresses. Ngrave traced bitcoin into 12 addresses, while XRP moved through 54 transfers. The company also acknowledged potential exposure of device information, wallet activity, IP addresses, and approximate locations, raising concerns about subsequent targeted scams.

The analytics firm Bitquery also published a report on the matter, noting that, in terms of the stolen funds, “most of it now sits on Hyperliquid as a Monero token.” The Bitquery report estimates around 81% found its way to the popular perps DEX exchange. In the incident report, Ngrave’s senior executive spoke on the matter.

Its CEO offered an unusually candid assessment, stating:

“In my humble opinion, the first duty of a crypto security company is to provide exactly that: security. In this, we have absolutely and utterly failed.”

He acknowledged that the company’s security posture was inadequate when he assumed leadership months earlier. Ngrave has since replaced compromised keys and outlined tighter notification controls, including two-person approvals, restricted domains and emergency shutdown capabilities.

Affected customers are being urged to establish fresh wallets and contact support. The investigation continues, leaving a troubling distinction intact: the hardware held firm, but the trusted messages surrounding it became the weapon.

It’s been a tough year for hardware wallet makers as 2026 has been riddled with security issues. Nearly a dozen documented hardware-wallet security incidents involving Ledger, Trezor, Tangem, Safepal, Bitbox02, and Coldcard. Reported losses exceeded $180 million across two incidents, exposing vulnerabilities in firmware, third-party vendors, physical security, and phishing, rather than direct remote attacks on recovery phrases.

title: Qubic restarts blockchain, opens recovery claims after $1.4M hack
summary: The network’s validators approved a recovery plan and opened claims until May 1, 2027.
content:
Layer-1 blockchain Qubic has restarted its network and launched a recovery process after a wallet seed vulnerability allowed an attacker to drain roughly $1.4 million in QU tokens from 1,404 accounts, according to the project’s latest update.

Qubic’s blockchain explorer shows the network resumed processing ticks 8:00 pm on Oct. 19, advancing beyond tick 85,371,949, where it was halted on Sunday.

Qubic said its network validators, known as Computors, had approved a recovery plan and that the project had launched a claims platform for affected wallet holders.

Affected users can check their address and submit a claim through Qubic’s reclaim platform. Affected users have until May 1, 2027, to submit claims, according to Qubic.

The network was halted Sunday to prevent further movement of stolen funds after attackers exploited predictable wallet seeds generated by vulnerable wallet software.

The vulnerability affected wallet seeds generated using Qubic’s web wallet on certain Apple devices and browsers, where an insecure random-number generator could produce predictable seeds. Qubic on Sunday said it had fixed the seed-generation flaw in the latest version of its web wallet. 

“If you created your wallet with the Qubic web wallet before version 4.26.4 (released 19 October), treat it as insecure, even if your funds were never touched,” said Qubic on Tuesday.

“Update to web wallet 4.26.4 or later, then create a new wallet,” said the team. “Move your funds to the new wallet as soon as you can, and never use the old one again.”

Related: Qubic freezes chain after attacker drains 1.4K wallets with weak seeds

title: Casper – Why AI Agents Need Their Own Payment Rails
summary: Michael Steuer is President and CTO of the Casper Association, the Swiss non-profit behind Casper Network, a proof-of-stake Layer 1 built for regulated real-world assets and payments between AI agents. Born in Amsterdam and based in Los Angeles for more than two decades, Michael has spent around 30 ...
content:
Skip to content

Michael Steuer is President and CTO of the Casper Association, the Swiss non-profit behind Casper Network, a proof-of-stake Layer 1 built for regulated real-world assets and payments between AI agents. Born in Amsterdam and based in Los Angeles for more than two decades, Michael has spent around 30 years in technology. That includes a stint as CTO for mobile at THQ, where his team shipped some of the first downloadable mobile games. He then co-founded Casper in 2018, built much of its ecosystem tooling through his company MAKE, and returned to lead the project in 2024.

The link will open a new window. Click the menu and down arrow to download the file.

Why you should listen

Casper’s origin story starts inside Ethereum’s own research group, where its proof-of-stake design was first developed. Michael and his co-founders wagered that enterprises would need something Ethereum wasn’t going to deliver quickly: a chain that companies with thousands of existing engineers could build on using the languages, testing and deployment processes they already have. Just as important was certainty. Michael explains why the probabilistic finality retail users tolerate, waiting through confirmations before an exchange releases funds, is unacceptable for an institution moving billions. During that window nobody can say who is legally responsible for the money, so Casper was designed so that a transaction belongs to the recipient from the very next block. He applies the same realism to tokenization. Minting a token that claims to represent an asset takes a minute, he says, but making that token confer enforceable rights is the hard part. Through the ERC-3643 standard and the T-REX Network, Casper is working to make compliance data, such as investor eligibility, jurisdictional limits and holding periods, travel with an asset as it moves between chains.

The second half of the conversation turns to what Michael sees as the larger opportunity. Cloudflare now reports that bots generate more web traffic than humans, yet almost no website can sell anything to them. Sign-ups, logins, card forms and terms-and-conditions boxes were all built for people. His answer is x402, a dormant payment code from the early HTTP specification that Coinbase and Circle revived as a standard for agents to pay per request. Casper is a founding member of the x402 Foundation, which now sits under the Linux Foundation, and settles those payments in its own dollar stablecoin, csprUSD. Payouts.com recently adopted Casper as the settlement rail for its AI agent products. Michael argues that companies blocking agents are turning away most of their visitors. He also expects stablecoin tribalism to disappear, because an agent shouldn’t care which dollar it spends.

That emphasis on ease of use is the thread through the final stretch. Michael says crypto’s usage remains in the single-digit percentages of the global population after 16 years largely because the industry made it so hard to use, from seed phrases to incompatible wallets, and warns against repeating that mistake with agents and tokenized assets. He makes the case for the CSPR token as a utility asset whose value tracks network usage, citing a staking yield he puts at around 10 to 11 percent alongside native liquid staking, and the recent Kraken listing for US access. In the hot take round he calls himself a multi-chain opportunist and argues that blockchain should never try to be the answer to everything. He predicts a decade defined by the convergence of TradFi and DeFi and by agentic traffic approaching totality. He also notes that most people don’t realize they can hold tokenized stock exposure in a wallet and borrow against it, and names Foundation as his sci-fi pick.

title: Quantum-Safe Blockchain Design Could Cut Fees and Network Bloat
summary: Upgrading blockchains to post-quantum cryptography typically causes severe network congestion, high gas fees, and state bloat due to massive signature and zero-knowledge proof sizes. Compact Shielded client-side validation (CSV) solves this problem by removing signatures from the blockchain and shif...
content:
Upgrading blockchains to post-quantum cryptography typically causes severe network congestion, high gas fees, and state bloat due to massive signature and zero-knowledge proof sizes. Compact Shielded client-side validation (CSV) solves this problem by removing signatures from the blockchain and shifting data storage and verification to end-user devices.

Key Takeaways

  • Dragos Ilie and his team at Imperial College London propose Compact Shielded CSV to solve quantum blockchain bloat.
  • The protocol shrinks on-chain data to 96 bytes and lowers network gas fees below current legacy chains.
  • Mobile wallets running STARK ZK proofs locally will verify incoming payments in under 100 milliseconds.

Eliminating Signatures: The 96-Byte On-Chain Footprint

For years, the cryptographic community has warned of an impending collision between quantum computing and blockchain technology. The math behind the threat is straightforward: public-key algorithms like ECDSA, which secure everything from bitcoin transactions to smart contracts, will no longer provide adequate security once quantum hardware matures.

Yet the proposed cure has often seemed almost as dangerous as the disease. Post-quantum cryptographic schemes routinely produce bloated signatures and massive zero-knowledge (ZK) proofs—a data explosion that threatens to clog peer-to-peer networks, overwhelm miners, and push up transaction fees.

However, a new architectural paradigm promises to break this zero-sum trade-off between quantum security and network scalability. Pioneered by cryptography researcher Dragos Ilie alongside a team from Imperial College London, Compact Shielded client-side validation (CSV) demonstrates that transitioning to post-quantum cryptography doesn’t require accepting exorbitant gas fees or sluggish network performance.

In fact, by reimagining how ownership is proven and offloading verification work directly to users’ devices, the protocol achieves an on-chain footprint far lighter than even today’s legacy blockchains.

At the core of the quantum scalability problem lies a traditional design choice: storing heavy digital signatures on a public ledger for every full node to check. Compact Shielded CSV abandons on-chain signatures entirely, replacing them with a novel cryptographic construct termed the degriefer.

In practice, a single-input transaction recorded on the blockchain consists of three concise 32-byte hashes totaling just 96 bytes: a nullifier to prevent double-spending, a transaction commitment, and the degriefer itself.

“The degriefer is just a hash over the coin’s nullifier, the owner’s secret key, and the transaction spending the coin,” Ilie explained. “By adding this little hash onchain, the sender can now construct an offchain zero-knowledge proof against it.”

Neutralizing Front-Runners and Griefing Attacks

Because constructing the accompanying ZK proof requires the owner’s secret key as a private input, malicious relayers and front-runners are mathematically dead-ended. “An attacker can frontrun a transaction, but he cannot construct a valid ZK proof, so for sure he cannot benefit from this,” noted Ilie.

Furthermore, if an attacker broadcasts a conflicting transaction to stall the spend, the legitimate owner can effortlessly unmask the attempt. “The user can ZK-prove the frontrunning transaction is an invalid griefing attempt by showing that his actual secret key hashed with the nullifier and attacker’s transaction does not produce the degriefer posted by the attacker,” Ilie emphasized.

Therefore, rather than forcing every node across the globe to download, execute, and archive every piece of transaction history forever, Compact Shielded CSV shifts the responsibility of storing and verifying proof data to the specific users involved in a transaction.

From an end-user perspective, operating a wallet on Compact Shielded CSV feels similar to using a lightweight Bitcoin SPV client. “It just needs connection to at least one honest node,” said Ilie. To confirm an incoming payment, the wallet checks the proof’s public parameters against on-chain data and validates the ZK proof locally. “For example, for a STARK ZK proof, even on a phone, [verification] takes under 100 milliseconds,” he added.

Generating an outgoing payment proof requires slightly more computation, but Ilie expects this to speed up as proving circuits mature. Crucially, because the architecture relies on constant-size recursive proofs, historical transaction depth never penalizes the edge user. Addressing concerns about storing post-quantum proofs off-chain, Ilie observed:

“The proofs are indeed larger than signatures and slower to generate and verify, but that’s only a burden when the whole network has to store and validate them. Because this is a client-side validation protocol, each user only stores, verifies, and proves only the coins they personally care about, which is very manageable.”

To put the storage footprint into perspective, Ilie said that “a photo on your phone is 20–40× larger than one proof,” adding that sending payments requires “less bandwidth and storage than sending a picture.”

Zero State Bloat

As transaction histories grow, traditional edge devices often suffer from state bloat. Under Compact Shielded CSV, however, light clients store zero transaction history beyond the constant-size proofs for their own unspent coins. “For anything else, such as checking whether a nullifier has a conflicting spend, it simply queries full or archival nodes,” Ilie pointed out, adding that “history growth does not affect the size of proofs or verification time at all.”

Contrary to the prevailing belief that quantum resistance leads to high network congestion and expensive fees, Ilie argued that Compact Shielded CSV is significantly more efficient than today’s non-quantum networks:

“Rather surprisingly, our scheme is far lighter and faster than even traditional chains rather than heavier. We would have much lower transaction fees and far less network congestion, not only while being fully post-quantum, but also compared to the status quo.”

title: Utah AG sues Kalshi, pursues profits from prediction market company
summary: Derek Brown likened the prediction market company to a “public nuisance“ that was “causing a significant and substantial ongoing harm“ to state residents.
content:
Update (Oct. 20, 9:53 pm UTC): This article has been updated to include a statement from Kalshi.

Utah Attorney General Derek Brown announced a lawsuit against Kalshi, its affiliates and two Susquehanna trading companies, alleging that the prediction markets platform had been facilitating illegal betting in the US state since 2024.

In a Tuesday press briefing, Brown said Utah officials had petitioned a court to compel the companies to return about $30 million to $60 million in profits they made through allegedly illegal event contracts. The Utah attorney general alleged that Kalshi illegally offered its services to more than 32,000 users in the state, resulting in significant losses.

“Under Utah law, I have determined that this operation is causing a significant and substantial ongoing harm to a significant number of Utahns,” said Brown. “And so today, we are asking the court to stop sports, elections, politics, culture and mention bets here in Utah.” 

Kalshi sued Utah in February after lawmakers passed a bill on betting on prediction markets as gambling under state law. In August, a judge ruled in favor of Utah officials, saying federal laws under the US Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) do not preempt state gambling laws. An appellate court also denied Kalshi’s request for an injunction in September, blocking the platform from operating during its appeal.

“Kalshi is a federally regulated financial exchange, like the stock market,“ Kalshi spokesperson Jacki McGavick told Cointelegraph in response to the Utah lawsuit. “Our customers trade with each other and set the prices. As a national derivatives market overseen by the CFTC, Kalshi answers to federal law, and no single state should have a veto over it. This latest state court action does not affect our ongoing federal litigation.“

Related: NFL backs New Jersey authorities in SCOTUS petition over Kalshi

Ongoing legal battles across the US

The civil lawsuit is one of many filed by US state authorities against prediction market platforms like Kalshi and Polymarket over alleged violations of state gambling laws, many involving sports betting. Officials in Arizona remain the only ones in the US pursuing criminal charges against Kalshi, but other states, including Michigan, Ohio, Kentucky, Nevada, Massachusetts, Wisconsin and New York, have filed civil suits against one or more prediction market companies.

The Utah lawsuit comes as the US Supreme Court considers whether to accept a petition to weigh in on New Jersey’s own case against Kalshi over allegedly illegal sports bets. The case, if accepted by the high court, could potentially resolve whether the purview of prediction market companies falls under state authorities or the CFTC, which claims “exclusive jurisdiction” over the platforms’ event contracts.

title: U.S. CFTC sets agenda for AI forum, exploring trading and agentic finance
summary: A Commodity Futures Trading Commission task force is scheduled for October 28 to talk about how the latest "super intelligence" technology may impact markets.
content:
Summary

  • The U.S. Commodity Futures Trading Commission released the agenda for its first "Frontier Forum" event next week, hosted by the agency's Innovation Task Force.
  • The October 28 event will invite leaders in the artificial intelligence space to discuss how AI may shift how the U.S. derivatives markets operate.

The potential effects of artificial intelligence in the derivatives markets will be in focus at the U.S. Commodity Futures Trading Commission's first in a new series of meetings hosted by its Innovation Task Force on October 28.

Using President Donald Trump's favored "super intelligence" descriptor, the agenda released on Tuesday marks the opening outing of what the regulator is calling its "Frontier Forum" series. It begins with a look at how derivatives markets may respond to the influx of machine intelligence and how the technology may impact price discovery and risk management.

"Super intelligence is poised to transform our financial markets,” said CFTC Chairman Mike Selig in a statement.

The task force said the event will hear from leaders in the space, including the heads of firms such as Ornn, Architect and Liquid Compute.

The event will also explore how traders' own AI agents may operate under CFTC regulations.

title: Liquid Network Announces Final Stages of Recovery Following Massive Hack
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

Liquid Network Announces Final Stages of Recovery Following Massive Hack 
One month after hackers pinched 4,000 bitcoins, the Liquid Network is up and running again. 
This post Liquid Network Announces Final Stages of Recovery Following Massive Hack  first appeared on Bitcoin Magaz...
content:
The Liquid Network on Tuesday said that things were up and running again, over one month after hackers stole 4,000 bitcoin, worth about $320 million at the time, from the network’s federation wallet before returning most of it in a “white hat” operation.

Writing in a blog post, the Liquid Network said that it was entering “the final stages of recovery with enhanced security.” 

Hackers in September stole 4,000 bitcoins from the federation wallet that backs the Blockstream sidechain. Blockstream was able to negotiate to get back most of the funds. 

“The final phase of restoration involves reestablishing the network’s full 1:1 bitcoin backing, followed by the controlled reactivation of Federation peg-outs for authorized PAK key holders,” the Liquid blog post read. 

“The Federation, Blockstream, and independent security experts have made substantial progress toward this objective, with the necessary technical infrastructure and safeguards now in place.”

The post added that it had introduced phased swaps again. Blockstream CEO Adam Back wrote on X on Tuesday that swaps were working again. 

Liquid is a layer-2 created by Blockstream that allows users to quickly move assets backed 1:1 with bitcoin. People can swap stablecoins for bitcoin and bitcoin on the Lightning Network on apps that support the Liquid Network. 

Hackers were able to get 4,000 bitcoins by exploiting an inflation bug on the Liquid sidechain to create over 4,000 LBTC — a token supposedly backed by bitcoin — that did not exist before and cash them out for real on-chain BTC. 

The hackers claimed to be white hat hackers who then had an exchange with Blockstream via messages written into Bitcoin blocks. Though critics argue they were not so ‘white’ since they kept 15% of the stolen funds, worth millions.

In one message, the hackers slammed Blockstream as “delusional, greedy, and arrogant,” and threatened to reveal all of Blockstream’s encrypted messages in the exchange unless the company paid the hackers 10% of the bitcoins as an official bounty. 

“You SHALL pay 10% using your own money as bug bounty or you will cause all your holders a 15% loss for your irresponsibility and stinginess,” the message read. 

The hackers are still holding onto around 600 bitcoins — or 15% of the total funds — worth close to $50 million at today’s prices as per the latest public knowledge. 

It is not clear if Blockstream reached a settlement with the hackers in private.

Mathew Di Salvo

Mathew is a reporter who's covered the space since 2019, reporting on everything from Salvadoran president Nayib Bukele's Bitcoin bet to crypto exchange FTX's bankruptcy.

title: UK Banks Flooded With Crypto User Complaints, Led by Lloyds and Barclays
summary: Evidence of banks restricting services for crypto asset users keeps piling up on both sides of the Atlantic. A new report highlights the difficulties U.K. customers have faced with specific banks. Earlier this year, Stand With Crypto in the UK (SWC), a British crypto asset lobby group, gave bitcoin ...
content:
Evidence of banks restricting services for crypto asset users keeps piling up on both sides of the Atlantic. A new report highlights the difficulties U.K. customers have faced with specific banks.

Key Takeaways

  • U.K. crypto asset users filed more than 10,000 bank restriction complaints in three months, with Lloyds, Barclays, and NatWest leading the list.
  • Some banks cap crypto transfers, while others ban them outright or lack clear policies.
  • Stand With Crypto urges banks to adopt case-by-case controls and regulators to clarify their obligations.

Earlier this year, Stand With Crypto in the UK (SWC), a British crypto asset lobby group, gave bitcoin and other cryptocurrency users a tool to file complaints against their banks for blocking or limiting money transfers to U.K.-registered crypto asset platforms.

More Than 10,000 Complaints in 90 Days

According to SWC, 9,803 individuals filed more than 10,000 complaints between May and August 2026. Lloyds Banking Group received the most complaints, at 2,297. Barclays ranked second with 1,569 complaints, while NatWest Group, which includes the Royal Bank of Scotland, ranked third with 1,278.

These are among the U.K.’s largest banking groups, with some of the biggest customer bases, which could explain why they received the most complaints.

Meanwhile, Virgin Money received 103 complaints and The Co-operative Bank received 76, accounting for about 1% each of the total. However, this doesn’t mean they are the U.K.’s most crypto-friendly banks, as both prohibit crypto asset transfers altogether.

Even Revolut, which offers its clients various crypto asset-related features, received more than 500 complaints.

Crypto Ban, Transfer Caps, or No Policy

During the campaign, people could select their bank and the type of restriction they faced, while also adding details about their specific situation.

It’s unclear how the complaints were resolved, as banks dealt with customers directly.

“But advocates have come back to Stand With Crypto and told them about their journeys, so we do know that banks have engaged with them on this,” SWC told Bitcoin.com News.

The organization also identified three approaches to crypto asset transfers among U.K. banks: blocking all transfers, imposing limits, or not stating a policy at all, as Revolut and Lloyds do. For example, Barclays and HSBC U.K. allow £2,500 per transaction and £10,000 per 30 days, while Monzo caps transfers at £5,000 per 30 days.

Case-by-Case Controls and More Clarity

The report has some caveats. For example, it doesn’t account for differences in bank size or explain why individual transfers were blocked. Still, it indicates that thousands of crypto asset users in the U.K. struggle with transfers to regulated platforms.

As SWC emphasized, published policies offer no guarantees, as banks can still block or delay transfers. This limits customers’ ability to switch to a more crypto-friendly bank.

“Consumer choice cannot operate effectively when consumers do not know what they are choosing between,” the lobby group, which counts crypto giants Coinbase, Gemini, and Blockchain.com among its partners, said.

The organization called on banks to adopt “risk-sensitive, case-by-case controls instead of blanket sectoral blocks,” and urged the Financial Conduct Authority and the Treasury to “clarify that sector-wide blocks are not a proportionate interpretation of regulatory obligations.”

Systemic Discrimination

Another report highlighted the systemic nature of banking restrictions in the U.K. In January 2026, the UK Cryptoasset Business Council said that, according to its survey, 40% of transactions to crypto exchanges are either blocked or delayed by banks.

As reported in July, British lawmakers began investigating whether banks were imposing excessive restrictions on crypto asset businesses. In August, they asked major banks whether the country’s incoming crypto framework would change how they treat regulated crypto asset firms.

The SWC report follows a U.S. Office of the Comptroller of the Currency report that found nine major American banks had policies that could restrict financial services based on political beliefs, religious affiliations or lawful business activities. The crypto asset industry was also affected.

title: Swiss Financial Regulator Gives Green Light to Country’s First Bitcoin ETF
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

Swiss Financial Regulator Gives Green Light to Country’s First Bitcoin ETF
Bitcoin exchange-traded funds were only available to institutional investors — until now. 
This post Swiss Financial Regulator Gives Green Light to Country’s First Bitcoin ETF first appeared on Bitcoin Magaz...
content:
Swiss financial regulator FINMA has approved the country’s first bitcoin exchange-traded fund for retail investors. 

The watchdog said Tuesday that the approval comes as people in Switzerland express a growing interest in crypto — particularly bitcoin. 

Bitcoin ETFs — particularly in the U.S. — have widened the scope of investors who can buy and sell the leading cryptocurrency. Via shares that trade on the stock exchange, investors can buy exposure to the biggest cryptocurrency in a safe and regulated way. 

“As early as 2021, FINMA authorised a fund for qualified investors that invests primarily in a basket of cryptocurrencies,” the announcement read. 

“As Bitcoin has a long trading history and a particularly high trading volume compared with other cryptocurrencies, FINMA has approved an exemption from the applicable risk diversification rules in this case.” 

It added: “At the same time, FINMA emphasises that investments in Bitcoin — even through an approved ETF — remain highly risky.” 

The announcement did not reveal which asset manager or bank would debut the product. Switzerland already has crypto ETFs limited to institutional or qualified investors on the market. 

In the U.S., bitcoin ETFs had the most successful debut in the history of investment vehicles when approved in 2024. 

Now, traders, institutions, and retail investors can quickly buy shares that track the price of the leading cryptocurrency and not worry about exchanges or storage of the digital coin. 

The funds, managed by Wall Street giants like BlackRock, Fidelity, and Morgan Stanley, manage over $97 billion in assets, according to CoinGlass data. 

Mathew Di Salvo

Mathew is a reporter who's covered the space since 2019, reporting on everything from Salvadoran president Nayib Bukele's Bitcoin bet to crypto exchange FTX's bankruptcy.

title: Bitwise, Hyperliquid seek SEC rule changes for token trading, airdrops
summary: The firms are seeking clearer guidance on the classification of crypto assets and secondary-market trading as the SEC’s public comment period comes to a close.
content:
Bitwise Asset Management and the Hyperliquid Policy Center are pressing the US Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) to revise its proposed crypto rules, seeking clearer guidance on token classifications, airdrops and secondary-market trading in comment letters submitted Monday.

The requests come as the SEC closes public comments Tuesday on its proposed Regulation Crypto Assets, which would create exemptions for qualifying crypto fundraising and a conditional safe harbor for tokens associated with investment contracts.

In an Oct. 19 comment letter, Bitwise Asset Management urged the SEC to clarify how investment managers should determine whether a crypto asset is subject to securities laws, arguing that managers need a standard they can apply using “publicly available information.”

The firm also sought clearer rules on when managers can rely on an issuer’s proposed Form TR filing, which would certify that an investment contract has ceased to exist, and how they should assess tokens when no such filing exists.

Source: US Securities and Exchange Commission

In a separate submission, the Hyperliquid Policy Center urged the SEC to broaden its proposed safe harbor, arguing that it could come too late in a project’s development. The group called for clearer protections for airdrops that reward network participation, as well as guidance on token buybacks.

Hyperliquid also warned that the proposal “fails to provide clarity” on whether unregistered intermediaries can facilitate token trading or whether tokens can trade freely through onchain protocols. It urged the SEC to address secondary-market transactions directly rather than leaving exchanges and decentralized trading venues facing regulatory uncertainty.

Related: House Finance panel chair says regulator actions on crypto ‘fall short’ of CLARITY bill

SEC proposal faces legal and investor protection objections

While industry participants sought changes to the proposed rules, former SEC enforcement official John Reed Stark and Duke University finance scholar Lee Reiners took a different position altogether. In an Oct. 16 comment letter, they urged the commission to withdraw the proposal entirely, arguing that it exceeds the agency’s statutory authority and would weaken investor protections.

Stark and Reiners said that existing securities laws and the Supreme Court’s Howey test already provide a framework for regulating crypto offerings. They argued that the fundraising exemptions would weaken investor protections, while the proposed safe harbor would allow issuers to effectively remove their tokens from securities oversight through self-certification.

The two also warned that adopting the rules in substantially their current form would invite an immediate legal challenge, potentially resulting in the framework being struck down.

With the public comment period closing Tuesday, the SEC will review the submissions before deciding whether to revise, adopt or withdraw the proposed rules. The commission has not announced a timetable for a final decision, and any final rule would require a commission vote before taking effect.

title: Bitcoin Treasury Strive Debuts New Preferred Stock With 15% Dividend
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

Bitcoin Treasury Strive Debuts New Preferred Stock With 15% Dividend 
Strive’s second preferred stock offering, SATS, debuted Tuesday on the Nasdaq. 
This post Bitcoin Treasury Strive Debuts New Preferred Stock With 15% Dividend  first appeared on Bitcoin Magazine and is written by...
content:
Bitcoin treasury Strive’s preferred stock, SATS, is now trading on the Nasdaq, according to the company. 

The stock debuted Tuesday and will pay a 15% dividend every business day, according to an announcement. 

Nasdaq-listed Strive said it closed its upsized initial public offering of 7,000,000 shares of SATS at a public offering price of $90 per share. 

It comes as public companies work to financialize bitcoin via different products. OG bitcoin treasury Strategy, which has five different preferred stocks, proposed daily dividends for its products last month. 

“The successful, upsized IPO of SATS marks a critical milestone in our strategy to maximize long-term total returns for our common equity investors,” Matt Cole, Chairman and CEO of Strive, said in a statement. 

The Nasdaq-listed Strive also has SATA, another preferred stock, which pays a variable dividend. 

Strive debuted as an official bitcoin treasury last year and is now the fourth biggest company in the space. 

Founded by former Ohio gubernatorial candidate and tech entrepreneur Vivek Ramaswamy, the company holds 36,818 BTC worth over $3 billion at today’s prices. The company on Monday announced another bitcoin buy of 4,045 BTC between October 12 and 16.

In January 2026, it completed the acquisition of Semler Scientific in an all-stock deal — the first instance of a publicly traded Bitcoin treasury company acquiring another such company. 

Like with other digital asset treasuries, the idea is that investors can get amplified returns from Strive’s stock. The company buys bitcoin with equity, and maintains a debt-free balance sheet: no bonds, no credit lines, and no leveraged positions that could trigger forced liquidation in a downturn. 

Strive is following in the footsteps of software company Strategy, which started buying bitcoin in 2020. Strategy is now the largest corporate holder of bitcoin, with 848,517 coins worth over $60 billion. 

Its five preferred stocks are STRF, STRC, STRK, STRD, and STRE. 

Strive’s stock, ASST, was trading 4% higher on Tuesday. 

Mathew Di Salvo

Mathew is a reporter who's covered the space since 2019, reporting on everything from Salvadoran president Nayib Bukele's Bitcoin bet to crypto exchange FTX's bankruptcy.

title: Esports Firm Ninjas in Pyjamas Boosts Bitcoin Mining Operation With Added Rigs
summary: NIP Group, the publicly traded parent company of esports powerhouse Ninjas in Pyjamas, is expanding its bitcoin mining operation through another major hardware acquisition, bringing its planned computing capacity to nearly 14 exahash per second (EH/s) as it accelerates its transformation into a digi...
content:
NIP Group, the publicly traded parent company of esports powerhouse Ninjas in Pyjamas, is expanding its bitcoin mining operation through another major hardware acquisition, bringing its planned computing capacity to nearly 14 exahash per second (EH/s) as it accelerates its transformation into a digital infrastructure company.

Key Takeaways

  • NIP Group said it is acquiring 4.47 EH/s of bitcoin mining capacity, expanding its total hashrate to approximately 13.85 EH/s.
  • The company expects to mine 195 BTC monthly at full deployment, up from its previous target of 160 BTC.
  • The esports giant is expanding beyond gaming, using share-funded bitcoin mining acquisitions to support its ambitions in AI, high-performance computing and digital infrastructure.

Ninjas in Bitcoin Mining

The Abu Dhabi-based company announced Tuesday that it has signed a definitive agreement to acquire operational bitcoin mining machines with a combined hashrate of approximately 4.47 EH/s. The acquisition, its third tranche of mining assets and first announced since 2025, would increase its total installed capacity to approximately 13.85 EH/s.

At full deployment, NIP Group expects its mining operations to generate approximately 195 BTC per month—currently about $16 million worth—although actual production will depend on factors including network difficulty, global hashrate, and operational conditions. That would put the company among the larger publicly traded bitcoin miners by computing capacity.

Under the agreement, NIP Group will issue up to 247.1 million Class A ordinary shares to the sellers in exchange for the mining equipment. The firm valued the deal at up to $27.3 million. The machines are already deployed and operational at hosting facilities, allowing the company to begin generating additional bitcoin immediately after the transaction closes.

The latest expansion builds on an aggressive push into cryptocurrency mining that began in July 2025, when NIP Group established an initial operation with approximately 3.11 EH/s of computing power.

By Nov. 2025, the company had announced plans to expand that capacity to 11.3 EH/s. The firm then said in Jan. 2026 that its bitcoin mining capacity sat at 9.66 EH/s, and that it had mined 151.4 BTC between Sept. and Nov. last year.

From Games to Bitcoin and Beyond

NIP Group, best known for its esports operations across competitive games including Counter-Strike 2 and League of Legends, has increasingly positioned bitcoin mining as a way to generate revenue and finance investments beyond gaming.

NIP Group Co-CEO Hicham Chahine told Decrypt in Nov. 2025 that the company intended to accumulate Bitcoin while selectively selling its holdings to fund operating expenses and business expansion. He also described plans to direct mining proceeds toward AI, gaming applications, and the company’s DOJO fan token ecosystem.

That broader strategy remains central to the latest acquisition, with management suggesting its growing computing footprint could eventually support AI and high-performance computing applications.

“We are rapidly executing on our digital infrastructure strategy with this third tranche of mining asset acquisitions,” Chahine said in Tuesday’s announcement.

The acquisition also highlights NIP Group’s reliance on equity issuance to finance its mining expansion, a strategy that allows the company to acquire equipment without an equivalent upfront cash expenditure, but can dilute existing shareholders. The agreement was dated Sept. 24 and remains subject to customary closing conditions. NIP Group expects the transaction to close within 10 business days after those conditions are satisfied.

title: Crypto’s 2026 shutdown wave claims 82 projects. What went wrong?
summary: Crypto projects are struggling to survive as falling revenues, depleted funding and security breaches force closures across DeFi, blockchain infrastructure and gaming.
content:
Crypto researcher Stacy Muur has identified 82 digital asset projects and protocols that have reportedly shut down in 2026, raising questions about the financial sustainability of businesses across decentralized finance, blockchain infrastructure and Web3 gaming.

The list, published on X on Tuesday, includes Balancer, Radiant Capital, Neon EVM and Step Finance, among dozens of others. Muur described the number of closures as unlike anything she had previously witnessed.

The shutdowns follow a prolonged bear market, with Bitcoin (BTC) retreating from its October 2025 record high above $126,000 to below $60,000 earlier this year, adding to the financial strain on projects already struggling to attract users and generate revenue.

Source: Stacy Muur

Ethereum layer-2 network Blast is among the most prominent casualties. As Cointelegraph reported, the project announced its shutdown earlier this month, citing no “credible path” to economic viability. The decision marked a sharp reversal for a network that once attracted more than $2 billion in deposits.

Other projects have encountered different problems. In February, Step Finance shut down following a major treasury breach, while Radiant Capital announced in June that it would wind down operations after failing to recover from a 2024 exploit. Meanwhile, Coinbase-backed Satori Finance ceased operations after concluding that its revenue could no longer support the business.

Related: $4.2B crypto bank Anchorage Digital cuts 17% of workforce: Report

Why are so many crypto projects shutting down?

Research published by DeFiLlama in August identified 100 crypto projects that had announced shutdowns in 2026, including 40 in the preceding 90 days. The findings suggest that many projects struggled to attract enough users or generate sufficient revenue to sustain operations.

The most commonly cited reason was a lack of product-market fit, followed by depleted funding, insufficient revenue and decisions to pivot to other products.

Collectively, the projects raised approximately $1 billion and generated $250 million in cumulative fees. Nine raised more than $50 million each, suggesting that substantial financial backing offered little assurance of long-term survival.

The most commonly cited reasons for crypto project shutdowns in 2026. Source: DeFiLlama

The closures come as crypto investment becomes increasingly concentrated. According to DeFiLlama, venture funding rose in the first half of 2026 compared with the previous year, even as the number of deals fell 80%. Meanwhile, mergers and acquisitions totaled 87 transactions at the time of the report, already 65% higher than the previous year.

Related: Crypto Biz: Wealthy investors are buying crypto, but their advisers aren’t sold

title: Mastercard Begins Rolling Out AI Agent Payments Service With Coinbase, Base
summary: Mastercard is beginning to open up a system that allows AI agents to autonomously purchase digital services using blockchain technology and stablecoins, marking another step toward a future in which software can conduct financial transactions without direct human involvement. Mastercard Opens Up Age...
content:
Mastercard is beginning to open up a system that allows AI agents to autonomously purchase digital services using blockchain technology and stablecoins, marking another step toward a future in which software can conduct financial transactions without direct human involvement.

Key Takeaways

  • Mastercard demonstrated autonomous AI payments, allowing agents to purchase digital services within approved budgets without human intervention.
  • Coinbase, Base, and BVNK provide crypto infrastructure, enabling blockchain settlement and stablecoin payments through the x402 protocol.
  • Mastercard launched early developer access, advancing its vision of AI agents conducting automated, low-value transactions across digital services.

Mastercard Opens Up Agentic Payments

The payments giant announced Tuesday that it completed end-to-end pilots of its Agent Pay for Machines platform with partners including Cloudflare, Ant International, AIsa, Base, BVNK, Coinbase, and Hype. Mastercard is also opening early access to developers, providing tools to build and test autonomous payment applications.

The technology allows AI agents to purchase services such as data, computing power, and image generation while operating within spending limits established by their human operators.

Mastercard showcased the system at Cloudflare Connect through a demonstration involving Hype, a marketing agency that uses AI agents to develop advertising campaigns.

In the demonstration, Hype tasked an AI agent with planning a promotional campaign for a protein bar launch. The agent identified services needed to complete the assignment, including social media research from AIsa and image generation through Cloudflare AI Gateway.

After receiving budget approval, the agent completed nine payments across the two providers, purchasing research and generating eight campaign images without establishing separate accounts or billing relationships.

The system relies on x402, an open payment protocol that allows online services to request payment using the HTTP 402 status code. When an AI agent encounters a paid service, it generates a digitally signed payment voucher within its authorized budget. The service provider verifies the voucher before delivering the requested service.

These transactions occur offchain, allowing payments to be authorized rapidly, while providers can aggregate vouchers and redeem them later. Crypto infrastructure plays a central role in the arrangement. Coinbase Developer Platform supplies wallet infrastructure, while the Coinbase-backed Ethereum Layer 2 network Base handles blockchain settlement.

BVNK—which Mastercard acquired this year for $1.8 billion—provides the agent wallet functionality and uses Mastercard’s Global Money Platform to facilitate payments and settlement in traditional currencies or stablecoins. Sellers can receive funds through their preferred payment methods.

The demonstration follows Mastercard’s June launch of Agent Pay for Machines, which introduced a framework for high-frequency, low-value transactions between autonomous software systems. The initiative initially attracted support from more than 30 industry participants, including Coinbase, Stripe, Ripple, Polygon, and the Solana Foundation.

AI Payments Go Mainstream?

Mastercard is positioning itself as a trust and authorization layer for an emerging economy in which AI agents independently purchase digital resources. The company said its early-access program now offers buyer- and seller-side APIs, developer documentation, and a testing environment.

Although the demonstrations establish the technology’s potential, broader adoption remains dependent on developers integrating the system and businesses trusting autonomous agents to manage expenditures.

The development also highlights a growing role for blockchain networks and stablecoins in AI-driven commerce, where automated software may need to execute numerous small transactions across different service providers.

title: Here’s what happened in crypto today
summary: Need to know what happened in crypto today? Here is the latest news on daily trends and events impacting Bitcoin price, blockchain, DeFi, Web3 and crypto regulation.
content:
Today in crypto, stablecoin transfers reached $891 billion in the third quarter as major US banks tested blockchain-based settlement, Bitget announced plans to acquire a Thai crypto exchange weeks after a $388 million hack and analysts said a Bitcoin rally could revive corporate treasury purchases following a sharp slowdown in the third quarter.

US banks test stablecoin payments as quarterly transfers hit $891 billion

Stablecoin transfer volume reached $891 billion in the third quarter of 2026, more than quadrupling since early 2023, according to a Coinbase-commissioned report conducted by The Block Research.

The report found that stablecoins processed more than $400 million in adjusted transfers per hour, with 73% of screened volume occurring outside traditional US banking hours, including weekends and holidays.

Institutional adoption is also expanding. Seven of the 10 largest US banks have tested stablecoins or tokenized deposits for settlement, while 30% of mid-market companies engaged in cross-border business are using or piloting stablecoins, up from 10% in 2024.

A separate National Cryptocurrency Association survey found that 42% of US adults would be more inclined to open an account or expand their relationship with a bank offering crypto services.

Despite rising transaction volumes, stablecoin supply has barely changed over the past year. According to DeFiLlama, the market’s capitalization stood at $301.4 billion on Tuesday, down approximately 0.6% from a year earlier.

Standard Chartered recently pushed its $2 trillion stablecoin market forecast from 2028 to 2030, citing slower supply growth.

Bitget plans Thai crypto exchange acquisition weeks after $388M hack

Crypto exchange Bitget has announced plans to acquire Thailand’s GMO-Z.com Cryptonomics, seeking to expand its Southeast Asia footprint weeks after a major hack impacting its hot and warm wallets. 

The proposed transaction involves BTGT Management (Thailand), a company in which Bitget says it holds an interest, according to an announcement shared with Cointelegraph.  The acquisition will allow Bitget to introduce its trading platform to Thai users.

“Thailand is an important part of Southeast Asia’s digital asset landscape, and this acquisition gives us a great opportunity to establish local operations in a thriving country,” said Bitget CEO Gracy Chen.

GMO Internet disclosed the proposed sale to BTGT Management in a Sept. 24 filing, targeting completion for Oct. 31. Bitget’s announcement identifies its involvement in the transaction.

The company declined to comment on how much interest in BTGT Management the company holds and the financial and ownership terms of the proposed acquisition.

Bitcoin rally could revive treasury buying, but easy-money days over

Corporate Bitcoin purchases could accelerate toward the end of 2026 and into 2027 if the cryptocurrency rallies, but investors are likely to be more selective about which treasury companies they finance, according to analysts. 

Speaking to Cointelegraph, Bitwise head of research Ryan Rasmussen said there was a broad slowdown in Bitcoin treasury buying in Q3. Strategy’s Bitcoin holdings increased by a net 1,666 BTC in Q3, down from 83,901 BTC in Q2, according to company filings. Other public companies added a net 5,617 BTC, compared with 45,725 BTC in the previous quarter, according to figures supplied by Rasmussen. 

Rasmussen said he expects a re-acceleration of corporate Bitcoin purchases to begin as early as this year. Bitfinex head of derivatives Jag Kooner said renewed buying could follow if treasury companies regain premiums to the value of their Bitcoin holdings, but cautioned investors have become more selective since the 2025 boom.

“Shareholders have seen premiums collapse and some companies sell into weakness. Investors are now pricing these businesses on funding costs, balance-sheet discipline and bitcoin per share,” said Kooner. 

“A rally could therefore restart buying, particularly among companies with credible financing structures but a return to last year’s indiscriminate capital raising looks unlikely.”

title: River Markets Targets Institutional Distribution Role for OG.com and Crypto.com
summary:

Under a memorandum of understanding...
content:
