Tuesday, 20/10/2026 | 19:11 GMT by Tanya Chepkova

  • River would provide the trading interface and risk tools, while OG.com supplies event contracts and Crypto.com Exchange supplies spot liquidity.
  • Institutional adoption is still early: a survey found that 9% of derivatives firms trade prediction markets.

River Markets is positioning itself as a central distribution gateway for institutional prediction markets, signing a preliminary agreement to route orders for both OG.com’s event contracts and Crypto.com’s crypto spot liquidity through a single trading interface.

Under a memorandum of understanding signed on 20 October, River would become a distribution channel for both venues, allowing hedge funds and quantitative desks to work with event contracts and digital assets through one interface.

Under the memorandum of understanding signed on 20 October, River would serve as an external distribution channel for both venues, pitching macro funds and systematic desks a unified order-routing layer.

The agreement builds on River’s $8.5 million funding round in August. The company raised the money to develop execution and prime-brokerage tools for firms trading across prediction-market venues, where positions and liquidity are often spread between separate platforms.

The proposed connection would add OG.com’s contracts to that network and extend River’s offering to crypto spot markets.

How the Three Platforms Would Connect

Under the plan, River would provide the client-facing platform, order routing and risk tools. OG.com would supply event contracts through its CFTC-regulated exchange and clearinghouse, while Crypto.com Exchange would provide digital-asset spot liquidity. The two venues would serve different parts of the proposed offering.

Hedge funds and trading desks will be able to access those markets through River’s existing workflow instead of building separate connections to each venue.

The arrangement would broaden the assets available through River, though the companies have not described a shared collateral or settlement system for spot trades and event contracts.

“As prediction market participants seek sophisticated strategies, this partnership enables institutional desks to manage broader digital asset exposure seamlessly on a high-performance, secure trading platform,” said Iskandar Vanblarcum, Managing Director of Crypto.com Exchange.

Institutional Interest Is Growing, but Participation Remains Limited

River is building for a market in which professional interest has begun to translate into trading. In a June survey, Acuiti and Singapore Exchange found that 9% of institutional derivatives participants were actively trading prediction markets, pointing to an emerging market.

Kalshi has also reported institutional activity. In a recent Finance Magnates interview, its Head of Institutional, Andy Ross, said firms onboarding to or already trading on the exchange collectively manage more than $1 trillion in assets.

He described institutions as a significant share of activity and said they frequently trade against one another.

River co-founder and CEO Oscar Levy sees a larger role for the products: “Prediction markets have matured from a niche asset class into essential information infrastructure for global macro and quantitative trading desks,” he said.

The connection to OG.com and Crypto.com Exchange has no announced launch date. For now, the MoU sets out a planned route to both markets; it does not mean River’s clients can already trade them through the new integration.

title: Brokers With Payment Cards Could Get Their Own iPhone Wallets Under UK Plan
summary:
Apple would have to open the iPhone's contactless payment technology to rival UK apps at lower fees, under proposals the Competition and Markets Authority (CMA) published today (Tuesday). The regulator said Apple's fees and access rules are blocking UK fintechs from building competing services.
No f...
content:
2026-10-20T21:09:35.915+02:00

Tuesday, 20/10/2026 | 19:09 GMT by Damian Chmiel

  • The competition regulator wants Apple to open contactless access at lower fees; no UK firm has a rival wallet yet.
  • Trading 212 and eToro already let clients spend from their accounts, while Apple warns of weaker privacy protections.

Apple would have to open the iPhone's contactless payment technology to rival UK apps at lower fees, under proposals the Competition and Markets Authority (CMA) published today (Tuesday). The regulator said Apple's fees and access rules are blocking UK fintechs from building competing services.

No firm has yet launched a wallet to rival Apple's in the UK, according to the CMA. In the European Union, Vipps, PayPal, Klarna, Curve and BBVA have all done so since Apple opened access there in 2024.

London's trading industry is coming home!

The proposed conduct requirement would make Apple offer host-based card emulation (HCE), which keeps payment data off the device. UK developers can currently use only the on-device secure element (SE).

The CMA would not set prices itself. It expects charges to be "substantially lower" than Apple's current fees. It did not publish them.

Contactless made up 39% of UK payments in 2025, up from 3% a decade earlier, according to UK Finance data cited by the regulator. A Which? survey found 62% of UK adults use a digital wallet , with Apple Wallet the most popular at 50%.

Brokers have moved into payments as well. Trading 212 rolled out multi-currency payment cards in May 2024, following eToro, Equiti and XS. Under the CMA plan, UK firms like these could seek the same access to offer tap-to-pay inside their own apps.

Five Rival Wallets Launched in Europe

The European Commission opened its own case against Apple in 2020 and put Apple's offer to open the iPhone's NFC chip out for market testing in January 2024.

Six months later, Brussels made the commitments binding, giving rival wallets free access to tap-and-go payments.

Norway's Vipps went live on iPhones in December 2024, the first alternative to Apple Pay, according to the CMA. PayPal followed in Germany, and London-based Curve launched Curve Pay on iOS across the European Economic Area in May 2025. Lloyds Banking Group agreed to buy Curve that November.

The UK plan stops short of the EU terms on price. The CMA expects Apple to keep charging for access, and said offering both standards would let UK firms roll out payment services already available in the EU.

"These proposals open the door to more innovation, more choice and economic growth," Sarah Cardell, chief executive of the CMA, said.

Cardell said "high fees, strict terms, and technical restrictions" had made it too difficult for challengers to compete. The regulator also listed digital IDs, travel passes, digital keys and account-to-account payments as services that wider access could support.

Apple faces a similar fight in the US, where a group of credit unions took the company to court in 2023 over its control of iPhone tap-to-pay.

Apple Pushes Back on Security

An Apple spokesperson said the CMA should not require the company "to adopt an approach with lower privacy and security protections," according to Reuters. Apple said it had already made contactless payments available to developers through NFC and the secure element.

That route opened to UK developers in 2024 and requires a commercial agreement with Apple. UK banks have worked within Apple's wallet, and Monzo became the first UK bank to offer monthly payments through Apple Pay in September 2024.

The Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) backed the proposals. It and the Payment Systems Regulator (PSR) began examining how the growth of digital wallets affects consumers and businesses in July 2024.

"Opening up this technology will also support the expansion of open banking," said David Geale, the FCA's executive director for consumers, payments and competition.

The CMA found in October 2025 that Apple holds substantial and entrenched market power over its mobile platform. That designation lets it impose conduct requirements under the Digital Markets, Competition and Consumers Act 2024.

The regulator ran a call for evidence on iPhone NFC access in June and July. The consultation closes on November 17, and the CMA said it would make a final decision after assessing responses.

title: Sleeping Bitcoin Giant Moves 500 BTC Worth $41M After 10 Years of Silence
summary: On Tuesday, as bitcoin’s price cruised comfortably above $82,000, a long-dormant wallet established on Jan. 1, 2016, stirred from its decade-long slumber, transferring 500 BTC for the first time in more than 10 years. The haul joins other recently moved coins that had long sat untouched, bringing th...
content:
1. News
  2. Featured
  3. Sleeping Bitcoin Giant Moves 500 BTC Worth $41M After 10 Years of Silence

Published:Oct 20, 2026, 2:35 PM EDT

On Tuesday, as bitcoin’s price cruised comfortably above $82,000, a long-dormant wallet established on Jan. 1, 2016, stirred from its decade-long slumber, transferring 500 BTC for the first time in more than 10 years. The haul joins other recently moved coins that had long sat untouched, bringing the month’s tally to 1,745.615 BTC worth more than $143 million.

WRITTEN BY

SHARE

Published: Oct 20, 2026, 2:35 PM EDT

Key Takeaways

  • A bitcoin wallet dormant since Jan. 1, 2016, transferred 500 BTC worth $41.33 million to Coinbase on Tuesday.
  • October has seen 23 dormant bitcoin wallets awaken, moving 1,745.615 BTC valued at over $143 million.
  • Arkham linked the 500 BTC transfer to Irish drug dealer Clifton Collins, marking the fifth such movement in 2026.

Editor’s Note: This second half of this article was updated on Oct. 20, 2026, at 2:55 p.m. to clarify that the 2016 wallet was linked to convicted Irish drug dealer Clifton Collins and that the 500 BTC transfer was attributed to Irish law enforcement.

Bitcoin’s Sleeping Giants Awaken as October Activity Accelerates

As of Tuesday, data compiled by btcparser.com, which monitors the reawakening of long-dormant bitcoin wallets across the Bitcoin blockchain, reveals that 23 old-school wallets have emerged from hibernation so far in Oct. 2026.

That activity translates into 971.445 previously dormant bitcoins changing hands since Bitcoin.com News published its Sunday report on sleeping bitcoins. The substantial increase in spending activity originated from two distinct wallets within the batch. The first transferred 411.45 BTC from a wallet established on Sept. 11, 2013.

Arkham Intelligence identifies the entity behind the address as an unidentified “BTC whale.” The transaction moved funds from a legacy address to a newer Segwit-format wallet, consolidating two unspent transaction outputs (UTXOs) in the process.

Irish Authorities Move $41M From Drug Dealer’s Lost Bitcoin Fortune

Then came Tuesday’s 500 BTC movement from the legacy wallet established in 2016. Unlike the 2013 transaction, this transfer was linked to convicted Irish drug dealer Clifton Collins, whose confiscated bitcoin holdings have been gradually recovered by Irish authorities. Arkham Intelligence identified the $41.5 million transfer as the fifth such movement this year, with the funds arriving at Coinbase.

Collins originally accumulated 6,000 BTC between 2011 and 2012 using proceeds from cannabis trafficking, later losing access to the private keys reportedly hidden inside a fishing rod case discarded at a landfill. Irish authorities, working with Europol, began recovering the inaccessible fortune earlier this year, with Tuesday’s transaction bringing the total moved to 2,500 BTC. Arkham believes law enforcement is responsible for the latest transfer, although officials have not independently confirmed this particular movement.

The remaining 3,500 BTC, valued at approximately $288 million, represents another extraordinary chapter in one of Bitcoin’s strangest lost-fortune sagas.

title: OKX-ICE co-chair Andrew Cuomo calls corporate objections a ‘natural response’ to tokenized stock plans
summary: The former NY governor, who co-chairs the joint venture between the crypto exchange and Intercontinental Exchange, said companies were expected to take a wait-and-see approach.
content:
Updated Oct 20, 2026, 4:13 p.m. EDTPublished Oct 20, 2026, 2:26 p.m. EDT

3 min read

Summary

  • OKX-ICE co-chair Andrew Cuomo called issuer objections to tokenized stock trading a “natural response,” saying companies were expected to take a wait-and-see approach.
  • Sixteen companies, including Microsoft, Alphabet and Goldman Sachs, have objected to trading on the planned venue under the SEC’s experimental framework.
  • Securitize and Vertalo executives said issuers need answers about pricing, investor protections, custody and shareholder rights as the new markets develop.

A growing list of companies rejecting tokenized trading of their shares is an expected part of testing a new market structure, Andrew Cuomo, co-chairman of the OKX-ICE joint venture, said after Microsoft, Alphabet and Goldman Sachs joined the objectors.

“This is a very natural response,” Cuomo, an OKX board member and former New York governor, said during a press call on Tuesday. “The model was designed to give companies the right to determine whether they want to opt in or opt out.”

“We always anticipated that, because this is such a dramatic and revolutionary change, many companies would want to wait and see how it goes rather than be the first to participate,” he added.

His remarks followed a Monday public notice showing 16 companies had objected to having tokenized versions of their shares traded on OKXICE, the planned venue from crypto exchange OKX and New York Stock Exchange parent Intercontinental Exchange (ICE).

Seven newly disclosed objectors — Microsoft, Alphabet, Goldman Sachs, Qualcomm, Caterpillar, McDonald’s and Western Digital — joined companies including Broadcom, Verizon and UnitedHealth.

The objections offer an early look at how companies are navigating a new market structure that could let U.S. investors trade stocks around the clock on blockchain plumbing. The SEC’s five-year “Innovation Exemption,” rolled out roughly a month ago, gives qualifying venues room to test trading through automated market makers and liquidity pools, while giving issuers a say in whether their shares participate.

Cuomo described that approach as a deliberately limited experiment, with caps on the number of stocks and trading volumes.

“There are limits on how many companies can participate and on the volume that can be traded, so by definition, it really is a sandbox — a model demonstration,” he said.

A learning curve for issuers

Carlos Domingo, CEO of tokenization firm Securitize, also said issuers’ concerns warrant attention.

“We think it's entirely reasonable for issuers to ask questions about how these new markets work, particularly around pricing, investor protections and shareholder rights,” Domingo said.

“There's an important education process underway, and issuers should understand that they have different options for participating in tokenization, including issuer-sponsored approaches.”

Securitize earlier this month announced an offering of 12 tokenized stocks for U.S. investors, with plans to make them available on OKXICE’s venue. Microsoft and Alphabet are among those stocks. Their objections to OKXICE do not, by themselves, establish opposition to Securitize’s separate offering.

Dave Hendricks, CEO and founder of Vertalo, an SEC-registered digital transfer agent and tokenization software platform, said the objections show the framework is functioning as intended.

“The 30-day objection window is the mechanism the SEC built in to give companies a say,” he said. “Issuers are using it.”

Hendricks also pointed to gaps in infrastructure connecting traditional exchanges with tokenized securities venues.

“Today there is no system that normalizes, harmonizes and synchronizes trading on the exchanges with trading on TSVs, and that enforces the thoughtful framework the SEC designed in the Innovation Exemption,” he said. “Until that process exists, more objections are the predictable result.”

Still, companies could reconsider as that infrastructure develops.

“It's important to note that an objection today, before the rails are in place to harmonize, may be an acceptance later.”

title: Outpoll Expands Beyond Prediction Markets With Crypto Futures Trading
summary: Mahe, Seychelles, 20th October 2026, Chainwire
content:
Skip to content

Mahe, Seychelles, 20th October 2026, Chainwire

Mahe, Seychelles, October 20th, 2026, Chainwire

Forecast an event, trade the asset it moves, and manage both from one app.

Today, Outpoll unveiled Trading, an integrated perpetual futures venue embedded directly into its prediction market ecosystem. Prediction markets, futures, and the Outpoll app now function seamlessly as a single service backed by a unified account balance. Traders can seamlessly analyze impending events, execute trades based on expected market movements, and consolidate all their positions under one dashboard.

Consider the conventional approach: anticipating an interest rate cut by the Federal Reserve may involve taking a position on one platform, switching tabs to open a separate exchange, transferring capital, and then entering a long or short position on the index. Outpoll streamlines this into a single continuous process. A unified account balance supports both a position on the Federal Reserve decision and a position on the SPX500, or a forecast on oil supply alongside a direct position on crude oil. Forecasts and hedges coexist in a single unified interface across web and mobile.

How Prediction Markets and Futures Differ

Prediction markets reflect market sentiment, whereas futures empower traders to capitalize on price action. Most platforms restrict users to one mechanism — prediction venues rarely feature leveraged instruments, while derivatives platforms lack event contracts. Outpoll bridges this divide, delivering both asset classes through a single account, shared balance, and unified application.

Available Trading Assets

Trading covers three asset groups, quoted against USDT and USDC:

  • Crypto: BTC, XMR, PUMPFUN and more, in total 80+ pairs
  • Stocks and indices: AAPL, MSFT, SPX500 etc., in total 20+ pairs
  • Commodities – 4 pairs

Every contract is perpetual, so there is no expiry to roll. Go long or short with leverage of up to 100x.

The Toolkit Traders Expect

  • Isolated and cross margin
  • One-way and Hedge mode, to hold a long and a short on one asset at the same time
  • Market, Limit and Stop Market orders, with Take Profit / Stop Loss and Reduce-Only
  • TradingView charts right in the order screen
  • A calculator that displays the estimated liquidation price before an order is placed.
  • A public API for algorithmic strategies

Availability

Trading is live now on the web at outpoll.com and in the Outpoll app (Google Play). Active users will find the new section in their account, running on the balance they already have. First users to sign up get a bonus using promocode “NEW100”, which can be spent either on a discount on trading fees or on increasing the size of a position. Terms are on the platform. 

About Outpoll

Outpoll is a single service for prediction markets and perpetual futures. Users trade the outcomes of real-world events in politics, economics, crypto, sports and culture, and trade perpetual futures on crypto, stocks, indices and commodities from the same balance, on the web and in the Outpoll app.

App: Download

title: Strive closes $630M SATS IPO, leaves Bitcoin allocation unspecified
summary: The Bitcoin treasury company could acquire an estimated 7,372 BTC with its net proceeds, potentially surpassing Metaplanet’s holdings if it allocates the full amount.
content:
Strive, the Bitcoin treasury company led by chairman and CEO Matt Cole, closed its upsized initial public offering of SATS preferred stock on Oct. 20, raising $630 million gross, according to the company’s announcement.

The company has not specified how much of the proceeds it will use to buy Bitcoin (BTC).

Strive sold 7 million shares at $90 each. The company estimated net proceeds of $608.15 million after underwriting discounts, commissions and expenses, according to BitcoinTreasuries.net. In an SEC filing, Strive said it intended to use the funds for general corporate purposes, including Bitcoin purchases, working capital, income-generating assets, capital expenditures, share repurchases and acquisitions.

SATS carry a 15% annual dividend on its $100 stated amount, equivalent to $15 per share annually if paid in full. Dividends are cumulative and payable when declared by Strive’s board. At the $90 IPO price, the stated dividend represents an annualized amount equal to 16.67% of the purchase price.

At an illustrative Bitcoin price of $82,500, Strive’s estimated $608.15 million in net proceeds could purchase approximately 7,372 BTC before fees. If fully allocated to BTC, the purchase would increase Strive’s reported holdings from 36,818 BTC to roughly 44,190 BTC, potentially surpassing Metaplanet’s reported 44,000 BTC.

SATS dividends are scheduled to be payable each business day beginning Nov. 9, subject to declaration. The first payment, if declared in full, will include accruals dating from the Oct. 20 closing.

Strive chief risk officer Jeff Walton said the company has no debt or maturities and is focused on a single obligation: paying dividends.

title: Bitcoin Could Outperform Most Assets, JPMorgan Says — But the Bank Still Won’t Recommend It
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

Bitcoin Could Outperform Most Assets, JPMorgan Says — But the Bank Still Won’t Recommend It
The bank has said bitcoin could do better than stocks and bonds over the next 10 years but says it is still too volatile. 
This post Bitcoin Could Outperform Most Assets, JPMorgan Says — But...
content:
JPMorganChase’s asset management division has said that while bitcoin is still too volatile to be recommended for strategic investors’ portfolios, the cryptocurrency could outperform most asset classes over the next 10 years.

In its 2027 “Long-Term Capital Market Assumptions” report, the bank said that while volatility in the biggest cryptocurrency’s price has dampened, it is “premature to consider BTC as a diversifier in a balanced portfolio.” 

JPMorgan, one of the world’s biggest banks, has utilized Bitcoin’s underlying tech — the blockchain — to debut its own products. But the multinational’s CEO, Jamie Dimon, has long been a Bitcoin skeptic.

“BTC currently lacks a clear role as a diversifier in balanced portfolios due to unstable correlations to other asset classes,” the report read. 

It added: “We see bitcoin as a speculative asset and a hedge against monetary easing.”

The report went on to show a graph with a base case for bitcoin returns beating stocks, bonds and gold. But it did add that the coin’s volatility could harm its role in portfolios. 

“But should volatility continue to decline and correlations to other asset stabilize, this may evolve in the future, particularly as regulation becomes clearer and liquidity and price discovery continue to improve,” it noted. 

For now, the report added, bitcoin “mostly trades like a high beta risk asset that tracks global money supply growth.” 

Bitcoin has become more popular on Wall Street, especially since the Securities and Exchange Commission green lighted exchange-traded funds to trade in 2024. 

President Donald Trump’s pro-crypto stance has also helped: regulators under the U.S. leader have taken a far more open approach to watchdogging the space since 2025. 

JPMorganChase boss Jamie Dimon has famously blasted Bitcoin, calling it a “hyper up fraud” and “pet rock” — adding that its only value is to criminals.

Still, he has praised the coin’s underlying technology, and lauded crypto products like stablecoins. 

Mathew Di Salvo

Mathew is a reporter who's covered the space since 2019, reporting on everything from Salvadoran president Nayib Bukele's Bitcoin bet to crypto exchange FTX's bankruptcy.

Tuesday, 20/10/2026 | 17:23 GMT by Tareq Sikder

  • Chesterman previously served as Chief Operating Officer of IG Institutional for about a year.
  • Lucian Lauerman was recently promoted to Chief Executive Officer of OANDA Europe Limited.

Mark Chesterman has stepped down as Chief Risk Officer at OANDA after seven years at the company, according to a LinkedIn post published today (Tuesday).

London's trading industry is coming home!

OANDA has also undergone wider leadership changes in recent months. In June, Lucian Lauerman was promoted to Chief Executive Officer of OANDA Europe Limited, following the appointment of FTMO founders Otakar Šuffner and Marek Vašíček as co-CEOs of OANDA after discussions with Gavin Bambury, who stepped down as CEO.

Chesterman Ends Seven-Year Tenure at OANDA

“Today was my last day at OANDA, bringing seven years to a close,” Chesterman wrote. He described the period as one of “almost constant change”.

He said his work at OANDA covered several areas, including mergers and acquisitions, trading operations, risk management and board governance. He also referred to global leadership responsibilities amid the growth of artificial intelligence.

Chesterman's LinkedIn profile lists Head of Trading as one of his roles at OANDA. He held the position for two years and nine months.

Led IG Futures and FX Business

Before joining OANDA, he spent ten months as Chief Operating Officer at Stater Global Markets, a prime-of-prime broker .

He spent more than 14 years at IG before moving to Stater Global Markets. His roles included Chief Operating Officer of IG Institutional, Global Business Development Officer, Head of Futures and FX, Chief FX Dealer and Dealer.

As Chief Operating Officer of IG Institutional, he worked on operational processes, client onboarding and credit risk policies for the institutional business. He held the position for eleven months.

He then served as Global Business Development Officer for two years and two months. His responsibilities covered strategy, product development, marketing and revenue growth across IG's institutional business and its MetaTrader 4 platform.

Before that, Chesterman spent three years and ten months as Head of Futures and FX at IG, overseeing trading strategy, client flow monetisation and product development across foreign exchange, index derivatives, commodities and interest rates.

He began his career at IG as a Dealer, a position he held for four years and seven months, before serving as Chief FX Dealer for three years.

title: Why Crypto Gaming Still Need Traditional Payment Rails
summary:
Cryptocurrency has given online businesses another way to move money. Bitcoin, Ethereum, stablecoins, and other digital assets can support cross-border transactions while appealing to customers who already own crypto. However,
The post Why Crypto Gaming Still Need Traditional Payment Rails appeared ...
content:
Cryptocurrency has given online businesses another way to move money. Bitcoin, Ethereum, stablecoins, and other digital assets can support cross-border transactions while appealing to customers who already own crypto.

However, even gaming hubs designed around cryptocurrency still depend on traditional payment infrastructure. Bank transfers, payment cards, digital wallets, and specialist processors remain important because most customers earn, save, and manage their money in government-issued currencies.

Crypto expands the entertainment cashier, but it does not replace the wider financial system.

Most Customers Start With Traditional Currency

Before depositing cryptocurrency, a player must first acquire it. That transaction usually begins with Canadian dollars, US dollars, euros, or another conventional currency.

Customers may purchase crypto through a bank transfer, payment card, centralized exchange, or payment app. The transaction therefore reaches the blockchain through a traditional payment method. The same process often happens in reverse when players convert digital assets back into funds held in a bank account.

For online gaming platforms, this means crypto cannot be the only convenient option. Many Canadian players want to deposit directly in Canadian dollars without purchasing a digital asset, creating a crypto wallet, selecting a blockchain network, or paying conversion fees. This demand supports specialist payment services that connect online accounts with familiar banking infrastructure.

Gigadat is a Canadian financial technology provider that helps participating online gaming hubs facilitate deposits and, where supported, withdrawals through online banking payment services. Websites providing analysis on the industry, such as Casino.ca track Gigadat casinos and compare deposit limits, withdrawal processes, and payment conditions, which shows how much demand exists for simple Canadian-dollar payments.

That demand explains why even crypto-focused platforms benefit from keeping traditional rails. Supporting both systems lets an operator serve experienced crypto users while staying accessible to customers who manage their money in conventional currency.

Crypto-Only Platforms Reduce Their Potential Audience

Cryptocurrency ownership has expanded significantly, but many people still do not use digital assets for routine payments. Some hold crypto primarily as an investment, while others remain unfamiliar with wallets, blockchain networks, and transaction fees.

A crypto-only platform  adds several steps to the registration and deposit process. A customer may need to open a wallet, purchase an asset, copy a deposit address, choose the correct network, and wait for blockchain confirmation.

Traditional payment methods are more familiar to most customers. Offering both fiat and crypto options lets a platform serve experienced crypto users without excluding people who prefer established financial services.

Stablecoins Still Depend on Fiat Infrastructure

Stablecoins are designed to maintain a value linked to an underlying asset, usually a conventional currency such as the US dollar. This makes them more practical for online payments than cryptocurrencies with fast-moving prices.

Even so, stablecoins rely on connections with the traditional economy. Customers need exchanges and payment services through which they can purchase or sell them. Operators also need banking relationships to pay employees, suppliers, taxes, software providers, and marketing partners.

A platform may accept and pay out stablecoins while calculating its revenue, liabilities, and operating costs in fiat currency. Its crypto payment system works alongside conventional financial infrastructure, not in place of it.

Regulation Requires Reliable Financial Records

Regulated online businesses must monitor payments whatever currency is used. Depending on the sector, operators may need to verify identities, check the source of funds, screen transactions, and flag unusual account activity.

Public blockchains create permanent transaction histories, but a wallet address does not reveal who owns it. Operators may use blockchain analytics to review wallet activity, but they still need verified customer information and effective compliance procedures.

Traditional payment providers already operate within identity and transaction-monitoring systems. Their records help operators investigate activity, handle payment queries, and respond to regulatory requests.

Cryptocurrency does not remove the need for financial checks. It typically adds another payment environment that the operator must monitor.

Customers Expect Support When Payments Go Wrong

Blockchain transactions are generally irreversible. This can reduce some forms of payment fraud, but it offers limited protection when a player enters an incorrect address, chooses the wrong network, or sends an unsupported asset.

Traditional payment systems provide familiar processes for failed transactions, refunds, account recovery, and customer disputes. They may also make it easier to trace delayed payments.

Platforms that accept crypto need to offer equally clear support. Customers should know about network fees, confirmation times, minimum payment limits, accepted assets, and what happens if they use an unsupported blockchain.

Operators Must Manage Price Volatility

The value of cryptocurrencies can change rapidly. A business holding a volatile digital asset may see its value fall before it pays suppliers or processes customer withdrawals.

Some operators manage this exposure by converting deposits into fiat currency or stablecoins. Doing so requires access to exchanges, custodians, liquidity providers, and banking partners.

Operators also need enough reserves across every currency they support. A hybrid payment system makes it easier to honor withdrawals while reducing reliance on the price and liquidity of a single digital asset.

The Future of Online Payments Is Hybrid

Crypto entertainment activities are unlikely to abandon traditional payment routes. The stronger model is a hybrid cashier combining cryptocurrency with cards, bank payments, digital wallets, and specialist services.

Blockchain networks can offer speed, international reach, and flexibility. Traditional rails provide familiarity, broader accessibility, regulatory connections, and established customer-support processes.

The future is not a choice between cryptocurrency and conventional banking. Online gaming hubs need both, because each system solves different problems and serves different customers.

title: The Coinbase allegations expose Bitcoin's corporate governance gap
summary: Corporate adoption of bitcoin will stall as long as companies can't show who controls the money, who approves its movement, or whether it's still there, argues Onramp CEO Michael Tanguma.
content:
Oct 20, 2026, 1:02 p.m. EDT

5 min read

BlockTower Capital founder Ari Paul publicly accused Coinbase of losing roughly $25 million of his firm's assets and concealing hacks totaling more than $1 billion across a dozen institutions. Coinbase flatly denies it, Paul says active litigation prevents him from publishing his evidence, and the industry has spent the weeks since arguing about who is telling the truth.

The argument misses the most uncomfortable fact in the story: nobody outside the two parties involved can check. That is a strange place to land for an industry built on an asset designed so that no one would have to take anyone's word for anything. A custodian holding assets for much of the market stands accused of billion-dollar concealment, and the only tools available for evaluating the claim are the accuser's credibility and the custodian's word. The lesson for every company holding bitcoin, or deciding whether to, is that bitcoin on a balance sheet presents a controls problem, and until a custody arrangement can answer the same questions a board asks about the company’s bank and brokerage accounts, who can move the money and who signs off, stories like this one will stay unanswerable.

The questions no board can answer

Every other account a company touches comes with governance as a default. A corporate bank account has named users, defined roles, approval rules on withdrawals and an audit trail that a controller can hand to an auditor. A brokerage account has the same. The moment a business buys bitcoin, all of that disappears into one of two places: a single exchange login or a hardware wallet in somebody's drawer.

Boards have noticed, and they’re asking questions. Who can move the asset? Who approves the movement? What happens when the person holding the credentials quits, gets phished, or dies? These are not hypotheticals. QuadrigaCX’s chief executive died in 2018, holding the only keys, and roughly $190 million in customer assets went with him, as the Ontario Securities Commission later documented. Prime Trust discovered in December 2021 that it could not open its own legacy wallets, and still could not 18 months later when Nevada moved to put it into receivership. Across most of the industry, the honest answer to all these questions is a shrug. Companies that wanted bitcoin on the balance sheet have walked away at exactly this point. When Deloitte asked 200 CFOs at billion-dollar companies what was holding them back, the complexity of accounting and controls came in at 42%, within a point of price volatility. The asset was rarely the hard part.

The problem is more acute now than at any point in Bitcoin's history, because the threat landscape is compounding from two directions. Bitcoin turns holders into physical targets, and that hasn't waited for a new price high. Jameson Lopp's public tracker now logs more than 360 known physical attacks since 2014, including 86 in 2025 and more than 60 so far this year. Coinbase made the risk concrete last year when criminals bribed its support staff and stole customer data, including names, addresses and balance information. The company estimated the breach could cost $400 million; security researchers called it a wake-up call because stolen account data exposes holders to real-world coercion.

On the digital side, artificial intelligence has industrialized the attack: cloned voices on the phone with the finance team, phishing emails indistinguishable from the chief executive's, social engineering that improves monthly. A business holding a bearer asset on a single credential carries that entire surface area on behalf of its employees and owners, for an asset where losses are often permanent.

Why the current fixes fail

The industry's existing answers all concentrate risk instead of distributing it. Self-custody concentrates it on one person, which is why corporate self-custody collapses into key ceremonies at every hire and departure and a controller praying the keyholder never leaves angry. Exchange custody concentrates it on one company, with the client holding neither the keys nor any way to see behind the login. Audits, trust charters and SOC reports test the custodian's own books and processes. None of them gives the client named users, approval rules on withdrawals, or a way to confirm the asset is there without asking. The shutdown of BitMEX after 11 years was a reminder of how routinely single institutions simply end. Proof-of-reserves attestations, the industry's favorite half measure, show a snapshot of assets without showing controls, and say nothing about who can move what tomorrow.

The durable fix uses properties bitcoin already has. Multiple signatures are native to the protocol, which means keys can be generated and held by independent regulated institutions, with no single institution able to move or lose the asset, the company holding legal title, named users with defined roles, approval policies on every withdrawal, and an audit trail a board can actually read.

Institutions are already moving in this direction. When Morgan Stanley designed custody for its proposed bitcoin ETF, it named two custodians rather than one, a sign that relying on a single custodian is now a live concern at the top of the market. But splitting custody only goes halfway. The real test is whether the owner can see for itself what it holds, without taking any custodian's word for it. Bitcoin makes that possible, and a custody setup that doesn't take advantage of it leaves the owner exactly where Coinbase's clients are today, waiting for someone to tell them the truth.

Single-custodians are, admittedly, convenient

The fair objection is that single-custodian arrangements exist for good reasons. They're simple: one counterparty to vet, one contract, one integration, and for many companies that simplicity is worth a lot. Spreading custody across independent institutions is harder than it sounds, requiring coordination, shared standards and operational discipline the industry spent its first 15 years avoiding.

Both points are true, and neither weakens the case. Simplicity is only an advantage if what's being simplified can be checked. A single custodian that can't show its clients what it holds hasn't removed complexity; it has hidden it. The cost of that only shows up when a question like the one facing Coinbase lands, and nobody outside can answer it. A financial system in which a billion-dollar question about client assets can't be settled from the outside has failed at the exact thing bitcoin was invented to fix. Building something better than a single point of trust is hard, and it's also the industry's actual job.

Verification was the whole point

Corporate adoption of bitcoin will stall as long as companies hold it in custody that can't show who controls the money, who approves its movement, or whether it's still there, which is exactly the gap the Coinbase allegations exposed. Boards do not need to become bitcoin experts to force the change; they only need to ask what they already ask of every other account, and add one more question: what survives the departure of any single person or institution. Any custody arrangement that cannot answer those questions clearly is a risk disclosure waiting to be written. A decade from now, the industry will look back with astonishment that it invented a radically new form of money and spent years custodying it behind a single login. The sooner custody is built so that no single party can lose, move, or lie about what it holds, the sooner the question hanging over the industry becomes impossible to ask.

title: Hyperliquid Policy Center Calls For Five Changes To SEC Crypto Rule
summary: TL;DR: The Hyperliquid Policy Center supports the SEC’s proposed crypto framework but says five changes are needed to make the rules workable for token developers and markets. The Hyperliquid Policy Center has welcomed the US Securities and Exchange Commission‘s attempt to clarify how securities law...

TL;DR: The Hyperliquid Policy Center supports the SEC’s proposed crypto framework but says five changes are needed to make the rules workable for token developers and markets.

The Hyperliquid Policy Center has welcomed the US Securities and Exchange Commission‘s attempt to clarify how securities law applies to crypto assets, while warning that details around distributions and trading could still create unnecessary barriers.

In a comment published October 19, the group urged the regulator to revise its proposed Regulation Crypto Assets framework in five areas. Its concerns include how administrative steps in token airdrops are treated, how tokens can trade after an exempt distribution, and whether a safe harbour offers clear enough protection once a project has matured.

The centre also wants clearer rules for token buybacks and a consistent approach to the interaction between federal exemptions and state securities requirements.

The proposals reflect a long-running problem for cryptocurrency developers. A network token may begin life inside a fundraising arrangement, yet eventually circulate in a system where thousands of participants trade and use it without dealing directly with its original issuer.

Drawing a line between those stages has been difficult under decades-old securities tests. The SEC’s proposal is intended to offer more predictable treatment, but the consultation process shows that industry participants still disagree about where the boundaries should fall.

The advocacy group’s submission is not a regulatory decision. It is one contribution to a rulemaking process whose final outcome will depend on the commission’s response to the evidence and objections it receives.

title: Bitcoin (BTC) Price Prediction: BlackRock’s $663M ETF Inflow Reverses October Outflows—Can BTC Break the $90K Barrier?
summary: Bitcoin (BTC) attracted renewed institutional interest on October 19 as BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT) recorded a substantial inflow, helping lift total net flows into US spot Bitcoin exchange-traded funds (ETFs) into positive territory for the session.
content:
Skip to content
Assets: BTC

Bitcoin (BTC) attracted renewed institutional interest on October 19 as BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT) recorded a substantial inflow, helping lift total net flows into US spot Bitcoin exchange-traded funds (ETFs) into positive territory for the session.

The development offered a fresh bullish signal as Bitcoin traded within $81.185–$82,954, although questions remain about whether demand can sustain a move toward $90,000.

Glassnode’s ETF flow data highlighted the surge, while market analysts pointed to Bitcoin’s daily Relative Strength Index (RSI), liquidation levels, and on-chain demand metrics to assess the recovery. Together, these indicators present a mixed picture: institutional buying has strengthened, but broader spot demand remains a key factor in determining whether the latest rebound can develop into a sustained advance.

BlackRock Bitcoin ETF Inflows Lift Market Sentiment

BlackRock’s IBIT attracted approximately $665.2 million on October 19, according to ETF flow data compiled by TFTC. However, outflows from Fidelity’s FBTC and Grayscale’s GBTC reduced the combined net inflow across US spot Bitcoin ETFs to approximately $526.6 million. This distinction matters because IBIT’s individual inflow was larger than the amount ultimately entering the entire ETF group.

U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs reported $663 million in inflows on October 19, led by BlackRock’s IBIT, though adjusted net inflows were closer to $527 million. Source: Glassnode via X

The daily inflow was the strongest since September, according to the supplied Glassnode analysis, and represented a significant change from the selling pressure seen earlier in October. However, the latest available figures showed that US spot Bitcoin ETFs remained down approximately $90.6 million for the month through October 19. The single-day inflow therefore narrowed October’s cumulative outflows but did not fully erase them.

The figures suggest that institutional demand may be returning, particularly through BlackRock’s fund. Yet one strong session does not establish a durable trend. Continued positive flows across multiple trading days would provide stronger evidence that investors are increasing their exposure to Bitcoin rather than making a short-term allocation.

Bitcoin Price Prediction: RSI Signals a Potential Recovery

Technical analysis shared by market commentator @Wealthmanager showed Bitcoin holding above a key daily support zone, with the 14-period RSI near 46. The indicator measures the strength of recent price movements and can help traders identify changes in momentum.

Bitcoin is holding above key daily support, while the 14-period RSI approaches levels that previously attracted buyers. Source: @Wealthmanager via X

The accompanying chart compares recent price action with earlier RSI divergences, highlighting periods when weakening downside momentum preceded price recoveries. If Bitcoin maintains support and the RSI begins moving higher, the setup could strengthen the case for a recovery. However, an RSI reading near 46 is not, by itself, a bullish confirmation. A sustained momentum shift and a break above nearby resistance would provide clearer evidence.

For the BTC price prediction, the immediate focus remains on whether buyers can defend the current support area and push the price above the recent trading range. Failure to hold support would weaken the recovery setup and could expose Bitcoin to another decline.

Bitcoin Price Faces a Key Test Above $84K

A CoinGlass liquidation heatmap showed Bitcoin advancing from around $81,000 to above $84,000, crossing a price area containing concentrated leveraged positions. Such heatmaps estimate where liquidation orders may cluster, helping traders identify levels where rapid price movements could trigger forced position closures.

Bitcoin’s liquidation heatmap shows a sharp rally from around $81,000 to above $84,000, breaking through a key liquidity level. Source: CoinGlass via X

A move above a heavily populated short-liquidation zone can accelerate gains if bearish traders are forced to close their positions by buying back Bitcoin. However, liquidation clusters do not guarantee a breakout, and the resulting momentum may fade once forced buying subsides.

The $84,000 area therefore represents an important near-term reference point in the supplied chart analysis. A sustained move above this zone could improve the technical outlook, while a rejection may leave BTC vulnerable to renewed consolidation. Reaching $90,000 would require Bitcoin to clear intervening resistance and attract sufficient follow-through buying.

Bitcoin May Be Entering an Accumulation Phase

Crypto analyst @misterrcrypto argued that Bitcoin’s current consolidation resembles the 2022–2023 accumulation period, when the market traded within a broad range before beginning a stronger recovery. The analyst’s chart identified a potential bottoming phase around $81,000 and suggested that prolonged sideways trading could precede another advance.

The attached chart overlays a “bottoming phase” box on 2026-2027 price action around $81,000, mirroring the 2022-2023 consolidation that preceded strong gains. Source: @misterrcrypto via X

Historical comparisons can help frame market scenarios, but they cannot establish that the same sequence will repeat. The duration of consolidation, investor demand, macroeconomic conditions, and the amount of available liquidity can all influence the next major move.

If Bitcoin continues to hold its recent support while buying pressure gradually improves, the accumulation thesis could gain credibility. Conversely, a breakdown below support would challenge the idea that the current range represents a durable market bottom.

Weak Spot Demand Remains a Risk for BTC

CryptoQuant’s apparent demand growth indicator continued to show negative readings in recent months, according to its latest analysis. The metric compares changes in Bitcoin supply with estimated demand to assess whether the market is absorbing available coins. Negative readings suggest that demand has not consistently kept pace with the supply entering circulation.

Bitcoin’s apparent demand growth has turned negative in recent months, indicating weak spot buying as prices consolidate near $80,000 in October 2026. Source: @cryptoquant_com via X

CryptoQuant contributor Rei Researcher noted that Bitcoin had recovered toward $82,000 even as apparent demand remained negative. The analysis indicated that demand had weakened since May 2026 and that short-term improvements had not yet produced a sustained reversal.

This creates an important distinction between a price rebound and a broader recovery. ETF inflows and short liquidations can support upward moves, but stronger spot buying would help demonstrate that investors are accumulating Bitcoin at current prices. Without that confirmation, rallies could remain vulnerable to profit-taking and renewed selling pressure.

Can Bitcoin Break the $90K Barrier?

Bitcoin’s near-term outlook depends on whether institutional inflows continue, technical support holds, and spot demand improves. BlackRock’s latest ETF inflow provides a constructive signal, while the move above $84,000 highlights the potential for derivatives positioning to amplify price changes.

Bitcoin (BTC) was trading at around $82,453 at press time. Source: Brave New Coin

However, the negative apparent-demand readings and October’s still-negative cumulative ETF flows show that the recovery remains unconfirmed. Traders will be watching for sustained ETF inflows, a stronger RSI, and a decisive break above nearby resistance before treating $90,000 as a more immediate target.

For now, $90,000 remains a potential upside objective for BTC price rather than a confirmed destination. A sustained move toward that level would require broader participation from spot buyers alongside continued institutional demand.

title: Injective, BDACS plan Korean won stablecoin settlement for tokenized assets
summary: Injective and BDACS plan to bring won-backed stablecoin KRW1 to tokenized asset markets as South Korea develops a regulatory framework for local currency stablecoins.
content:
Blockchain network Injective has entered into a memorandum of understanding with South Korean digital asset custodian BDACS to bring a won-backed stablecoin to its tokenized asset markets, potentially allowing institutions to settle transactions without relying on US dollar stablecoins.

According to a Tuesday announcement, BDACS’s KRW1 stablecoin would serve as the exclusive won-denominated settlement asset for real-world assets (RWAs) on Injective, allowing institutions to trade and settle tokenized assets directly in Korean won.

BDACS says KRW1 is fully backed by Korean won reserves. Minting and redemption would initially be limited to approved institutional partners, subject to regulatory approval.

The agreement comes as South Korea develops rules for won-backed stablecoins under its proposed Digital Asset Basic Act, which the government aims to finalize by the end of 2026. In the meantime, the country’s five largest crypto exchanges recorded net stablecoin outflows for 18 consecutive months through June, according to industry data cited by Cointelegraph.

Injective is a layer-1 blockchain that has increasingly focused on tokenized assets. In August, its institutional services arm registered with the US Securities and Exchange Commission as a transfer agent, allowing it to maintain ownership records and facilitate securities transfers. Injective’s native token has a market capitalization of roughly $887 million, according to CoinMarketCap data.

Related: China’s P2P stablecoin wallets surge 43x, Korea’s $450B crypto economy: Asia Express

South Korea moves toward won-backed stablecoin regulation

South Korea is still debating who can issue won-backed stablecoins as lawmakers work on the Digital Asset Basic Act. 

A July policy report by Hashed Open Research and the Solana Policy Institute called for greater flexibility in stablecoin issuance and interim licensing guidance while the legislation is being developed. The proposed law would establish a broader framework for digital assets, covering stablecoin issuance, disclosures and market rules.

South Korea’s efforts follow the passage of the US GENIUS Act, which established a federal regulatory framework for payment stablecoins, and the European Union’s Markets in Crypto-Assets Regulation (MiCA), which includes rules governing stablecoin issuers.

Industry data shows the stablecoin market remains overwhelmingly dollar-denominated, with US dollar-backed tokens accounting for more than 99% of the total supply.

Related: Mastercard launches stablecoin risk screening for banks and payment providers

title: BlackRock Files for Bitcoin ETF With Downside Buffer and Capped Upside
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

BlackRock Files for Bitcoin ETF With Downside Buffer and Capped Upside
A new filing with the SEC shows BlackRock wants to release an exchange-traded fund that offers downside protection but also caps gains. 
This post BlackRock Files for Bitcoin ETF With Downside Buffer and Capped ...
content:
BlackRock has filed for a new bitcoin exchange-traded fund which, if approved, would cap investors’ upside while limiting their losses. 

The iShares Bitcoin Managed Protection ETF, or PBIT, would aim “to create and manage bitcoin exposure,” according to a Monday filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission. 

It would work buying options and fixed-income strategies to give investors regulated bitcoin exposure with capped upside and some downside protection — but not direct bitcoin ownership. 

The fund would suit investors who want to invest in bitcoin but not experience all the volatility that comes with the top cryptocurrency. 

Bitcoin has attracted attention for its wild price swings over the years but its volatility has dampened as more investors have bought into the space. 

But 2025 was the least volatile year for the asset and the bear market of 2026 has been its most shallow on record: in past cycles, bitcoin’s price has dropped as low as 80% from its all-time high; this year it shed just 50% of its value. 

BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust — IBIT — started trading in 2024 after the SEC gave the green light to 11 spot bitcoin ETFs. 

The most successful of the ETFs in terms of flows, the investment vehicle has helped bring bitcoin to Wall Street. Now traders, institutions and retail investors can quickly buy shares that track the price of the leading cryptocurrency. 

They don’t need to worry about exchanges or storage of the digital coin, rather, BlackRock buys and holds the bitcoin while investors simply hit the buy or sell button via their brokerage account. 

IBIT has the most assets under management out of the bitcoin ETFs, currently handling $65.7 billion. 

On Monday, the fund received $665.2 million in fresh investment as bitcoin buyers flooded back into the market. 

That’s the biggest number of shares bought in the product since October 2025, when bitcoin notched a new all-time high, according to Farside Investors data. 

Mathew Di Salvo

Mathew is a reporter who's covered the space since 2019, reporting on everything from Salvadoran president Nayib Bukele's Bitcoin bet to crypto exchange FTX's bankruptcy.

title: Webull Partners with Kalshi to Add Crypto Perpetual Futures in the US
summary:
Webull plans to begin offering perpetual futures to eligible US customers in November, starting with Bitcoin and selected other crypto assets. The broker expects broader availability before year-end, although it has not announced a specific launch day. 
Customers approved for futures trading will ac...
content:
2026-10-20T18:26:00.000+02:00

Tuesday, 20/10/2026 | 16:26 GMT by Tanya Chepkova

  • Eligible customers will use existing futures accounts; Kalshi will list and clear trades.
  • Leverage and fees remain undisclosed; funding payments and liquidation rules apply.

Webull plans to begin offering perpetual futures to eligible US customers in November, starting with Bitcoin and selected other crypto assets. The broker expects broader availability before year-end, although it has not announced a specific launch day.

Customers approved for futures trading will access the contracts through their existing Webull Futures accounts. The rollout adds another leveraged product to a platform already offering conventional futures, stocks, options, cryptocurrency and prediction markets.

Global perpetual futures trading volume exceeded $90 trillion in 2025, according to Anthony Denier, Webull’s Group President and US CEO.

"As this market continues to grow, we believe U.S. investors should have access to perpetual futures through a regulated platform they already know and trust, bringing a product with significant global adoption into the U.S. regulated futures market," he added.

Perpetual Futures Will Use Existing Webull Accounts

The contracts will be listed on KalshiEX, a designated contract market regulated by the Commodity Futures Trading Commission, and cleared through Kalshi Klear, its regulated clearing organisation, while Webull Futures will provide brokerage access.

The broker plans to add further products, subject to regulatory review and exchange listing requirements.

Perpetual futures have no fixed expiry date, removing the need to roll positions into replacement contracts. However, holding a position involves periodic funding payments, and Webull warns that positions can be automatically liquidated if margin falls below maintenance requirements.

The company also states that futures accounts are not protected by the Securities Investor Protection Corporation (SIPC).

A Brokerage Channel for Kalshi’s Derivatives

Kalshi received CFTC approval for its Bitcoin perpetual futures contract in May 2026. Webull’s planned rollout adds a brokerage distribution channel for these derivatives, with Kalshi supplying the exchange and clearing infrastructure.

On 6 October, Kalshi launched a perpetual contract, which references the MerQube US Large Cap Index, and covers the 500 largest US-listed and US-domiciled companies.

Webull has confirmed cryptocurrency contracts for the initial rollout. It has not said whether Kalshi’s US 500 contract or other non-crypto perpetuals will be available through the broker.

TL;DR: Super League shareholders have approved proposals connected to Metaplanet’s plan to contribute 2,100 BTC and cash to a new US-listed Bitcoin treasury platform.

Metaplanet’s proposed American Bitcoin treasury vehicle has moved a step closer to reality, but the transaction has not yet closed. Super League Enterprise said shareholders approved the relevant proposals at their annual meeting on October 16, clearing an important hurdle in the arrangement announced earlier this year.

Under the deal, Metaplanet’s US subsidiary would contribute 2,100 Bitcoin and $2.5 million in cash to Super League. After closing, the Nasdaq-listed company is expected to change its name to Superplanet and trade under the ticker SUPA.

The arrangement gives the Japanese Bitcoin treasury specialist a potential US capital-markets platform, while Super League would retain its existing advertising and media business as an operating segment.

Importantly, the shareholder vote is not the same as completion. Regulatory filings, Nasdaq requirements and other customary closing conditions remain outstanding, with the companies currently targeting the fourth quarter.

The proposed structure also raises questions that extend beyond the Bitcoin price. Investors will need to watch how ownership is allocated, how additional capital could be raised and whether the operating business changes the risk profile of a Bitcoin-heavy public company.

For now, the news is a procedural milestone in an unusual cross-border deal — not evidence that 2,100 BTC has already arrived on the balance sheet.

TL;DR: Bitmine says its Ethereum holdings reached approximately 6.04 million ETH after it added 12,535 tokens over the past week.

Bitmine Immersion Technologies has pushed its Ethereum treasury past the six-million-token mark, reporting holdings of 6,041,481 ETH as of October 18. The company said it acquired another 12,535 ETH during the preceding week.

The size is striking even by corporate crypto-treasury standards. Bitmine describes its position as roughly 4.9% of Ethereum’s circulating supply and says more than five million of its ETH are staked.

That staking component matters. Unlike a Bitcoin treasury that generally depends on price movements, a large Ethereum holding can also earn network rewards by participating in validation. Rewards are not risk-free, however, and the economics depend on staking performance, technical operations and protocol conditions.

Bitmine valued its wider portfolio of crypto assets, cash, marketable securities and other investments at about $15.1 billion. Its holdings therefore represent a substantial bet on Ethereum as both a long-term asset and a productive network.

The company’s disclosure offers investors a clearer look at the scale of that wager, though headline token counts are not the same as shareholder returns. Equity valuation, financing arrangements and the market price of ETH all affect what ownership in the company is ultimately worth.

As more listed firms build dedicated crypto treasuries, those distinctions are likely to become increasingly important.

title: Sui Price Prediction: Bullish Fractal Emerges Around $0.99—Is SUI Near a Bottom After Falling From $1.25 to $0.95?
summary: Sui (SUI) is showing mixed technical signals after retreating from $1.25 to approximately $0.95, with the token trading near $0.99 in the latest chart analysis provided.
content:
Skip to content
Assets: SUI

Sui (SUI) is showing mixed technical signals after retreating from $1.25 to approximately $0.95, with the token trading near $0.99 in the latest chart analysis provided.

While a bullish fractal on the three-day Sui chart points to a possible recovery, shorter-term Elliott Wave analysis suggests that selling pressure may persist before a clearer reversal develops.

The next key levels are $0.95 support and $1.05 resistance. Market participants are watching whether SUI can maintain its support base and break above resistance, which could strengthen the case for a recovery. However, a developing bullish pattern does not confirm that the correction has ended.

SUI Price Prediction: Bullish Fractal Faces a Critical Test

A three-day Coinbase chart shared by crypto analyst @lourenco_vs highlights a potential bullish fractal, with converging trendlines and labeled Elliott-style waves suggesting that the market structure may be approaching a turning point. The chart also identifies fair value gaps (FVGs), which traders monitor as potential areas of price imbalance.

The 3-day Coinbase chart shows SUI near $0.99, with FVGs, Elliott wave patterns, and converging trendlines signaling a potential bullish fractal. Source: @lourenco_vs via X

The analysis emphasizes the importance of assessing the broader timeframe rather than interpreting every short-term pullback as evidence of renewed weakness. After an extended decline, traders may react cautiously to price fluctuations, even when higher-timeframe charts begin to show signs of stabilization.

Nevertheless, the fractal remains a technical interpretation rather than confirmation of a trend reversal. SUI would need to establish stronger price action around support and overcome nearby resistance before the bullish scenario gains further credibility.

Elliott Wave Analysis Warns of Further Downside

A separate four-hour analysis presents a more cautious outlook. According to the accompanying Elliott Wave interpretation, SUI has continued to follow a bearish scenario after declining from the top of Wave D. The developing structure now appears to be forming either a symmetrical or diametric pattern, with price moving through Wave E.

The pattern now suggests a symmetrical or diametric structure, with the SUI price currently progressing through Wave E. Source: behdark via X

Within this larger formation, Wave E may itself be developing into a diametric pattern. The analysis suggests that Wave G of E remains incomplete, leaving room for another downward move before the broader structure progresses into Wave F.

The projected green zone is identified as a potential area for Wave G to end. A move into that region could also sweep a previously identified liquidity pool, making it an area to monitor for a possible reaction. However, the source analysis does not provide a specific price level for this zone, so its exact location cannot be established from the available information.

The trading framework outlined in the analysis favors watching for potential short positions between the current price and a higher red zone, with the green zone as a downside target. If SUI reaches the green zone and subsequently produces a confirmed bullish reaction, the red zone becomes a potential recovery target.

These scenarios depend on how price behaves at the identified zones. The Elliott Wave count may also change as new candles develop, so the projected sequence should not be treated as a confirmed outcome.

SUI Support at $0.95 and the $1.05 Breakout Level

Crypto analyst @CryptoMichNL argues that SUI may have completed its correction from $1.25 to $0.95. The analysis links the decline to a broader market pullback, noting that Bitcoin fell approximately 10% from $87,000 during the period under review.

SUI may have completed its correction from $1.25 to $0.95 amid Bitcoin’s 10% decline from $87K, as altcoins typically face deeper volatility-driven selloffs. Source: @CryptoMichNL via X

Altcoins can experience sharper price swings during broad market corrections because liquidity conditions and investor risk appetite affect their performance. SUI’s decline therefore needs to be assessed alongside the wider cryptocurrency market rather than in isolation.

The $0.95 area is the key support level highlighted in the supplied analysis. Holding above it would keep the potential recovery scenario in consideration, while a decisive break below support could expose SUI to additional downside. The available sources do not establish a confirmed lower target.

On the upside, $1.05 is the principal level to watch. A sustained move above this threshold could provide stronger evidence that buyers are regaining control and potentially open the way toward higher resistance levels. Until that breakout occurs, the possibility of another rejection or a period of consolidation remains.

Macro Outlook: Bitcoin’s Pullback Adds Pressure to Altcoins

Bitcoin’s reported decline from $87,000 provides important context for SUI’s recent weakness. When the largest cryptocurrency retreats sharply, altcoins can face additional selling pressure as traders reduce exposure to riskier assets.

Bitcoin (BTC) price chart. Source: Brave New Coin

The relationship is not uniform, and Bitcoin’s direction alone cannot determine SUI’s next move. Still, a broader market recovery would provide a more supportive backdrop for a bullish fractal to develop, while renewed weakness across major cryptocurrencies could undermine attempts to hold support.

Traders assessing SUI’s outlook should therefore consider both its individual chart levels and the wider market trend. A recovery in Bitcoin could help improve sentiment, but SUI would still need to demonstrate its own strength by defending support and reclaiming resistance.

Looking Ahead: Can SUI Confirm a Reversal Near $0.99?

SUI’s current technical picture remains divided between a potential bullish fractal on the three-day chart and a bearish Elliott Wave structure on the four-hour timeframe. The difference highlights why signals across multiple timeframes may not align during a correction.

Sui price chart. Source: Brave New Coin

The immediate focus remains on the $0.95 support area and the $1.05 resistance level. Holding support and breaking above resistance would strengthen the recovery case. Conversely, continued rejection below $1.05 or a loss of $0.95 would weaken the argument that SUI has established a durable bottom.

For now, the available chart analyses point to a market at a potential decision point rather than a confirmed reversal. A sustained breakout, stronger follow-through, and improving broader market conditions would provide more convincing evidence that SUI is preparing for another advance.

title: Cross River Buys the Front End of a Wallet It Was Already Powering
summary:
Cross River plans to expand what it offers merchants by acquiring Accrue, a wallet technology company for which it already provides banking services. 
The deal would combine the bank’s regulated infrastructure with a product that lets consumers store money, receive rewards and make purchases through...
content:
2026-10-20T16:32:13.481+02:00

Tuesday, 20/10/2026 | 14:32 GMT by Tanya Chepkova

  • Cross River already holds funds and issues cards for Accrue’s wallets.
  • The deal would let it offer the wallet and banking services together to merchants.

Cross River plans to expand what it offers merchants by acquiring Accrue, a wallet technology company for which it already provides banking services.

The deal would combine the bank’s regulated infrastructure with a product that lets consumers store money, receive rewards and make purchases through a merchant’s website or app.

CRB Group, the parent of Cross River Bank, has agreed to acquire Accrue for an undisclosed sum. The transaction is subject to customary closing conditions.

According to Accrue's programme terms, the bank holds customers' deposited funds and issues the linked Visa debit card. Accrue supplies the interface that merchants embed in their websites and apps. In effect, Cross River is buying the customer-facing layer of a product it already helps run.

One Product from Banking to Checkout

Customers fund Accrue Balance from a bank account or card and spend it with the participating merchant. The wallet shows rewards and refunds next to deposited funds, so customers can see what they have available at checkout.

For merchants, the main draw is keeping the money after a return. A customer can take a refund into the branded balance instead of back to the original payment method, then spend it on another purchase.

“Payments and loyalty are becoming one,” said Gilles Gade, Founder and CEO of Cross River. “Every brand wants its own wallet, and with Accrue, all of our clients can now build one on our platform. We never stop innovating, and we are excited to work with Michael Hershfield and his team to help our clients build the financial super apps of the future.”

This broader use of stored value grew out of Accrue’s original “save now, buy later” product, launched in 2021. The service helped customers accumulate money for purchases while earning merchant-funded rewards.

Accrue has since extended the wallet to handle more of the payment relationship between a merchant and its customers.

If the acquisition closes, merchants could obtain the wallet alongside the banking and payment services Cross River already provides. Accrue’s team will join the bank, with founder and CEO Michael Hershfield taking a leadership role in building out that offering.

TL;DR: Strive purchased another 1,223 Bitcoin over two days, taking its reported holdings to 36,818 BTC in a fresh SEC filing.

Strive’s Bitcoin buying spree continued through the middle of October. In a filing dated Monday, the company disclosed the purchase of 1,223 BTC between October 14 and October 16, bringing its total reported holdings to 36,818 coins.

The latest purchase cost roughly $100 million at an average price of about $81,734 per Bitcoin, according to the company’s figures. It followed an earlier acquisition of 2,822 BTC in the same week, showing how aggressively the corporate treasury strategy has accelerated.

The size of the holding puts Strive among the largest publicly traded Bitcoin owners. That creates an unusual relationship between the company’s shares, its balance sheet and the price of Bitcoin: investors are evaluating not only the coins it holds, but also how management finances future purchases.

Preferred shares, equity issuance and other capital-market tools are increasingly central to the treasury-company model. They can give firms more ways to acquire Bitcoin, but also raise questions around funding costs, dilution and the risk of buying into volatile markets.

Strive’s announcement does not tell us where Bitcoin prices go next. It does, however, give a clear snapshot of one company’s conviction and the increasing scale of its exposure.

The key metric for shareholders will be whether that accumulation creates value per share, not just a larger total Bitcoin balance.

TL;DR: AnchorWatch has opened its Nevada-chartered Bitcoin custody service, pairing a choice of key-control structures with optional Lloyd’s-backed insurance.

Bitcoin custody is no longer just a question of who holds the private keys. For professional trustees, company treasuries and advisers, it also involves governance, recoverability and what happens if assets are lost through theft or coercion.

AnchorWatch Trust Company has entered that market as a Nevada-chartered qualified custodian. The company is offering a model in which it controls the keys required for custody while clients can retain additional signing authority, alongside a second arrangement distributing key control among AnchorWatch, BitGo and CoinCorner.

The firm says eligible customers can apply for insurance backed by Lloyd’s of London syndicates. Its launch announcement described a possible limit of up to $370 million per client, although coverage depends on underwriting approval and the terms of an individual policy. This is not blanket protection automatically attached to every Bitcoin in custody.

Pricing is also part of its pitch. AnchorWatch is positioning fixed-dollar custody charges, with a monthly ceiling of $10,000, against the percentage-based pricing common across institutional asset services. Insurance costs are separate.

The structure is aimed at customers who want the controls of regulated custody without concentrating every signing decision in a single institution.

Ultimately, the value of any such product depends on the actual key arrangements, policy exclusions, service reliability and how clearly clients understand the risks that remain uninsured.
