title: GRVT Burns 1.1 Million Tokens as Countdown to Grvt 2.0 Begins
summary: Singapore, Singapore, 20th October 2026, Chainwire
content:
Skip to content

Singapore, Singapore, 20th October 2026, Chainwire

Singapore, Singapore, October 20th, 2026, Chainwire

The discretionary buyback represents close to 1% of circulating supply and precedes four planned product milestones culminating in Grvt 2.0.

Grvt, a self-custodial trading platform built on its own zero-knowledge (ZK) chain, announced that the Foundation’s token issuer has completed its first GRVT token buyback, purchasing and burning 1.1 million GRVT tokens on the open market.

The transaction permanently removed close to 1% of GRVT’s circulating supply at the time of purchase. It marks the first of five milestones ahead of the planned launch of Grvt 2.0 at the end of November 2026.

A Discretionary Buyback with On-Chain Verification

The Foundation’s token issuer intends to conduct further buybacks on a monthly basis. Each transaction remains entirely at the issuer’s discretion, with no predetermined purchase amount or guaranteed schedule.

Buybacks are executed through an independent execution partner, with purchased tokens transferred to a designated burn address and permanently removed from circulation.

The transactions can be independently verified through the public buyback dashboard, which records the number of tokens purchased and burned, the percentage of circulating supply represented, cumulative burns and on-chain transaction hashes.

“The GRVT token is an important part of the ecosystem we are building,” said Hong, co-founder and CEO of Grvt. “We welcome the issuer’s buybacks as a demonstration of its long-term commitment to the ecosystem and community. Grvt is expanding its products and markets, and the issuer’s buybacks sit alongside that as a supportive mechanism aimed at reducing circulating token supply.”

Grvt Outlines Four Product Milestones

The announcement follows GRVT’s token generation event in July 2026 and precedes a series of planned launches.Grvt Earn, scheduled for the End of October, will introduce yield opportunities backed by tokenized assets, with target yields of up to 11%. Potential returns are expected to derive from underlying asset cash flows, including interest, premiums and invoice-related income. Asset-supplying partners will be announced at launch. Target yields are not guaranteed.

Stable Funding Perps, scheduled for November, will introduce perpetual futures linked to commodities, stocks, foreign exchange and indices. The contracts are planned to carry zero trading fees and use once-daily funding. Grvt aims to list more than 1,000 markets by the end of December 2026.

Yield as Margin, also scheduled for November, will allow eligible Grvt Earn balances to support trading positions while continuing to accrue yield, subject to applicable product terms and risk parameters.

Grvt 2.0, scheduled for the End of November, will consolidate these capabilities into a single self-custodial app, alongside a new name, visual identity, and the company’s 2027 roadmap.

Addressing Idle Capital

The expansion follows a survey of Grvt traders conducted earlier in 2026. Six in ten respondents reported keeping at least a quarter of their capital on the platform idle, while many reported moving funds elsewhere to pursue yields of 8% or more.

Grvt’s upcoming products aim to reduce the separation between earning yield and deploying capital for trading.

“Traders shouldn’t have to choose between putting their capital to work and keeping it ready to trade,” Hong said. “Grvt 2.0 is designed around a single self-custodial balance that can support both activities.”

Founded in 2022, Grvt currently supports perpetual futures across approximately 200 cryptocurrency and real-world asset markets.

The GRVT token launched in July 2026 and confers no ownership, profit or other economic rights.

Further details are available in the full announcement.

About Grvt

Grvt is a self-custodial trading platform operating on its own zero-knowledge chain. The platform supports cryptocurrency and real-world asset perpetual futures and is developing products that allow eligible balances to earn yield while supporting trading activity.

Learn more at grvt.io.

TL;DR: The Blockchain Association has urged the US Treasury to draw clearer lines around DeFi software, foreign stablecoin issuers and who could face liability under proposed GENIUS Act rules.

The fight over US stablecoin regulation is shifting from Congress to the details of implementation. In comments on Treasury’s proposed Section 3 rules under the GENIUS Act, the Blockchain Association has argued that a framework designed for regulated payment issuers should not inadvertently catch unrelated software and market participants.

One sticking point is the definition of a digital asset service provider. The association wants officials to distinguish customer-facing financial businesses from infrastructure such as self-custody software and validators that do not provide the same services.

It also disputes how the rules might define knowing participation in unlawful stablecoin issuance. Its position is that enforcement should require genuine knowledge and meaningful assistance, rather than interpreting ordinary secondary-market activity as evidence of involvement.

Foreign-issued stablecoins are another concern. The group says compliance requirements should rely on accessible regulatory information rather than assuming every service provider can investigate an issuer with which it has no direct relationship.

These are advocacy positions, not changes Treasury has adopted. Regulators still have to balance the industry’s request for workable rules against their responsibility to police payment products and financial crime.

The eventual language will help determine whether GENIUS Act compliance is mostly a challenge for stablecoin issuers or one that reaches much further into the surrounding ecosystem.

Tuesday, 20/10/2026 | 12:34 GMT by Tareq Sikder

  • The acquisition plan comes weeks after a $388 million security incident.
  • Recently, the firm listed Thailand, Russia, Belarus and Kazakhstan among its restricted jurisdictions.

Bitget plans to acquire Thailand-based digital asset exchange operator GMO-Z.com Cryptonomics, weeks after a security incident affected its hot and warm wallets.

The proposed deal follows Bitget's recent announcement that it would discontinue services for certain users in what it described as a “one-off exercise.”

London's trading industry is coming home!

Bitget's terms of use, updated earlier this month, list Russia, Belarus, Kazakhstan and Thailand among the jurisdictions where its services are prohibited.

The acquisition could provide a route into the Thai market through a locally licensed operator, although Bitget has not explained whether the deal would change its existing restrictions or how it would structure its services in the country.

Acquisition Involves BTGT Management

The transaction involves BTGT Management (Thailand), in which Bitget says it holds an interest. GMO Internet disclosed the proposed sale in a filing earlier this month, with completion targeted for the end of the month.

Bitget CEO Gracy Chen said the acquisition would support the company's plans to establish local operations in Thailand.

Bitget has not disclosed its ownership interest in BTGT Management or the financial terms of the proposed deal.

GMO-Z.com Cryptonomics operates Z.com EX, which launched in 2021. Thailand's Securities and Exchange Commission lists the company among its licensed digital asset exchange operators.

The transaction remains subject to regulatory approval and other conditions.

Find out more 👇 https://t.co/s1Kw9I0FNi

Security Incident Affected Approximately $388 Million

Last month, a security incident disclosed by Bitget last month. The exchange said attackers exploited a vulnerability in a third-party security product to issue fraudulent withdrawal commands, affecting approximately $388 million.

Bitget said customer account balances were unaffected. It completed the phased restoration of withdrawal services earlier this month.

TL;DR: Mesh and Visa have announced a partnership intended to let consumers spend cryptocurrency and stablecoins from participating wallet apps wherever Visa payments are accepted.

Holding stablecoins is one thing. Actually spending them in a shop usually involves moving funds to an exchange, selling them, or relying on a separate payment product. Visa and Mesh are pitching a way to make that process less visible to the customer.

Under their newly announced partnership, Mesh’s payment infrastructure will connect eligible crypto wallet balances with Visa’s acceptance network, spanning more than 175 million merchant locations. The ambition is to support both online and in-person spending without requiring customers to manually cash out their tokens first.

Visa supplies the acceptance infrastructure. Mesh provides the orchestration layer responsible for connecting wallet balances to a payment made in the currency a merchant expects to receive.

It’s a potentially significant distribution arrangement for digital asset payments, but the announcement is not the same as saying every crypto wallet already works in every shop. Participating apps, market availability and the precise rollout remain important variables.

For merchants, the appeal is continuity: they would interact with an established payments network rather than needing to accept a particular blockchain asset directly. For wallet providers, the attraction is a more everyday use for balances that often stay within crypto trading platforms.

The test will be whether the experience is genuinely as simple as a conventional card payment once the integration reaches customers.

title: France's parliament approves vote to hit stablecoin trades with 31% capital gains tax
summary: Amendment I-3898 removes tax deferral for MiCA-compliant stablecoins starting January 2027.
content:
Summary

  • French lawmakers approved taxing crypto-to-stablecoin swaps at the 31.4% capital gains rate.
  • Amendment I-3898 removes tax deferral for MiCA-compliant stablecoins starting January 2027.
  • Critics warn the levy may push traders toward DeFi platforms and offshore exchanges.

French lawmakers narrowly approved a proposal to tax gains when investors swap cryptocurrency for stablecoins, bringing the transactions a step closer to falling under the country’s 31.4% capital gains levy.

The National Assembly adopted amendment I-3898 to the 2027 budget on Oct. 16 by 38 votes to 37, with 25 abstentions. The vote advances a proposal previously approved by its finance committee.

The proposed changes would apply to transactions from Jan. 1, 2027. They remain subject to the budget’s remaining parliamentary stages and could still be amended or removed before becoming law.

Exchanges between crypto without an additional cash payment generally benefit from tax deferral under current French tax rules. Taxable gains on private investments face a default rate of 31.4%, although investors can opt for the progressive income-tax scale.

The amendment would remove that deferral when investors receive e-money tokens as defined by the European Union’s Markets in Crypto-Assets (MiCA) framework.

Investors could therefore owe tax on gains when moving into qualifying stablecoins, even without withdrawing the funds in fiat currency to a bank account.

The proposal has drawn warnings about its effect on trading. Francois Volpoet, Chainalysis’ regional sales director for France, told CoinDesk last week that it could push investors toward decentralized finance platforms, peer-to-peer transactions and offshore exchanges outside international tax-reporting arrangements.

Public Accounts Minister David Amiel raised questions about implementation and asked for the amendment to be withdrawn, opposing it otherwise.

“We first need to define stablecoins, then ensure our ability to monitor and trace reallocations within a portfolio of assets,” he told lawmakers during the parliamentary debate.

The finance committee’s rapporteur general, Philippe Juvin, said he favored keeping the deferral given crypto’s volatility.

The text would also replace France’s portfolio-wide capital-gains calculation with one based on the acquisition cost of the assets sold, using a weighted average for units of the same cryptocurrency bought at different prices.

title: Equity weakness could damp demand for bitcoin after biggest ETF inflows in a month

Summary

This is an excerpt from CoinDesk newsletter 'Daybook.' Sign up here, if you haven't already.

Bitcoin BTC$82,846.65 dropped about 1.1% over the last 24 hours, ether ETH$2,450.67 fell 1.7% and the broader CoinDesk 20 (CD20) Index lost roughly 1.6%, pulled lower by declines in Asian stocks and the rising price of oil.

Further weakness in equities could damp demand, analysts at QCP Capital wrote in a note published Monday. That may be on the cards. Both Nasdaq 100 futures and S&P 500 futures are lower, with companies including Coinbase Global COIN$170.74·Market Closed and Galaxy Digital GLXY$15.75·Market Closed falling in pre-market trading.

“Broader equity deleveraging dynamics could transmit to cryptocurrency markets and potentially threaten the $80,000 support level if sustained,” the analsysts wrote.

For the time being, the bitcoin price remains above that level after demand for the largest cryptocurrency picked up on Monday, as illustrated by the spot U.S. bitcoin ETFs. The funds posted their biggest net inflows in a month and BlackRock’s IBIT recorded its largest inflows in over a year.

Monday’s fund flows offer encouragement for bulls, though demand remains concentrated. The ETFs attracted roughly $527 million in net flows, with BlackRock’s taking in $665 million while those from Fidelity and Grayscale recorded withdrawals.

The ether ETFs lost $103.3 million, their fourth consecutive day of outflows, showing bitcoin-specific demand rather than demand for the wider crypto sector.

Conversely, the analysts added, a continued Treasury rally could support risk assets, particularly alongside falling real yields and a weaker dollar.

Even so, the macro backdrop leaves little room for complacency. The U.S. 10-year Treasury yield is around 5.13%, while Brent crude is trading near $110 a barrel, keeping energy-driven inflation risks a headwind that could worsen if the geopolitical backdrop doesn’t improve.

The Federal Reserve is widely expected to hold interest rates steady next week, though a 25 basis-point increase is being priced in for next month on prediction markets, leaving little reassurance for investors worried about tightening conditions. Stay alert!

  • U.S. CFTC rebuffs CME legal stance in consequential fight over perpetual futures (CoinDesk): The Commodity Futures Trading Commission argued CME lacks standing to challenge its perpetual futures policy because it has failed to demonstrate financial harm.

  • Stock futures mixed as chip stocks come under pressure in premarket (CNBC): AI-linked stocks came under selling pressure before Tuesday’s open, after a mostly higher session on Wall Street.

TL;DR: Mastercard has launched Stablecoin Security, a risk-scoring tool designed to help financial institutions examine payments before and during their movement across blockchains.

Stablecoin transfers can settle quickly. Investigating a suspicious payment before it happens is a much harder task, particularly when the transaction crosses providers, blockchains and traditional banking systems.

Mastercard wants to tackle that problem with Stablecoin Security, introduced at Money20/20 in Las Vegas. The product combines conventional payment intelligence with blockchain data so banks and payment companies can assess fraud, sanctions and scam risks across a transfer’s journey.

The service works through an API and can generate a risk assessment before a transaction is completed. Mastercard says it can consider the payment context, the origin of the funds and potential exposure to restricted parties. Borderless.xyz and Keyrails are the initial partners.

For businesses considering stablecoin settlement, this fills an operational gap. A payment may be technically possible and still raise questions about counterparties, compliance or whether the funds arrived through a compromised wallet.

Mastercard’s announcement cites research covering 593 million stablecoin transfer events and 141 million Ethereum transactions in 2025, finding that almost 60% involved more complex, multi-step routes rather than simple one-to-one transfers.

The company is initially launching in North America and expects wider commercial availability in 2027. It isn’t promising to eliminate fraud, but it is bringing a familiar banking control into an increasingly unfamiliar payment environment.

title: “You Want to Go to the Place That’s Got All the Liquidity”: Kalshi’s Andy Ross on Its Pitch to Brokers
summary:
Build or rent? FX and CFD brokers looking to add event contracts face a familiar infrastructure choice: build their own venue or connect to an existing one. For Kalshi’s Head of Institutional Andy Ross, the answer starts with liquidity: “You want to go to the place that’s got all the liquidity.” 
Th...
content:
Build or rent? FX and CFD brokers looking to add event contracts face a familiar infrastructure choice: build their own venue or connect to an existing one. For Kalshi’s Head of Institutional Andy Ross, the answer starts with liquidity: “You want to go to the place that’s got all the liquidity.”

The liquidity argument also explains why broker distribution matters to Kalshi: each new connection can bring more participants to the same order book.

London's trading industry is coming home!

Ross said firms onboarding to or already trading on Kalshi collectively manage more than $1 trillion in assets. He described institutional involvement as a ‘significant proportion’ of activity and said institutions frequently trade against other institutions.

The broker channel, however, is only one part of its institutional strategy. The exchange is also adding perpetual futures, including planned FX products, and offering market data to firms that may use its prices without trading the underlying contracts.

Why Building an Exchange Does Not Build Liquidity

Kalshi has begun distributing its event contracts through existing brokerage platforms.

An API-based service launched with Apex Fintech Solutions allows brokers to add the contracts to their own interfaces without creating their own exchange and clearing infrastructure. tastytrade was the first broker to go live.

When asked why a broker should connect rather than build or acquire an exchange, Ross focused on order concentration.

He said that Kalshi’s advantage is the concentration of users “not just through brokers but directly on its platform” and institutional channels, which together are “creating this phenomenal price point.”

Similar event contracts may be available on several venues, but differences in settlement terms and wording can make them non-identical.

“You’ve got to be able to check: is the contract exactly written the same?” Ross said. “But if the products are somewhat analogous and there’s liquidity, then you can go trade on those if you want.”

“You want to go to the place that’s got all the liquidity and all of the pricing and all of the depth in the order book, so that when you put the trade on, you can also get out of the trade,” he added. “It’s important to be able to do that.”

How Brokers Can Add Prediction Markets

The Apex arrangement shows how a broker can give clients access to Kalshi’s order book without operating an exchange itself.

The broker retains its interface and customer relationship, Apex handles clearing, custody, money movement, statements and account management, while Kalshi operates the regulated marketplace and lists the event contracts.

“That client then can use that broker interface and stay in that broker’s ecosystem to be able to get access to prediction markets or get access to the perpetuals that are trading on Kalshi,” Ross said. “The client doesn’t have to go and sign up to seven new places if they want to do that, and so they get a consolidated risk report.”

For the broker, this expands the product range while keeping the customer on its platform. For Kalshi, it brings additional participants and fee-paying order flow.

“We offer an order book, and more people who come to trade on it, we get paid fees for that, obviously,” Ross said. “The quality of the market goes up. Therefore, trading volume goes up.”

He described the arrangement as a “win-win-win” for the customer, broker and exchange.

Why Kalshi Is Expanding Beyond Event Contracts

The products available through Kalshi are also expanding beyond the event contracts on which the exchange built its business.

“People don’t just want prediction markets,” Ross said. “They also want to be able to trade on leveraged delta in perpetuals. And so we’re offering both.”

Kalshi has launched perpetual futures on cryptocurrencies and precious metals, extending the range on 6 October with US500, a contract linked to an index of 500 large US companies.

Today we launched the first stock index perpetual future in America. You can now trade a perp on the US 500, an index of America’s largest companies weighted by market cap. Stock index perps let you trade the broader market with greater capital efficiency and make it easier to do things like take a short position. Unlike traditional options and futures, they don’t expire, so there’s no need to roll over contracts or decide when to exercise an option. Gains and losses are tied directly to how much the market moves, giving you an efficient and straightforward way to ask the question: is the market going up or down? One perpetual contract concentrates liquidity instead of spreading it across expiration dates. Bringing more traders and competing views into a single liquidity pool on a national exchange can strengthen competition, improve pricing, and make markets more efficient over time. This launch brings us closer to building a financial exchange for anyone and everyone. Prediction markets gave traders exposure to the events that move the stock market. The US 500 is the natural next step: a way to trade on the market itself.

— Kalshi (@Kalshi) October 6, 2026

The company is looking to add FX perpetuals, although Ross did not identify the potential currency pairs or provide a launch timetable.

“We’re looking to launch FX perpetuals,” Ross added. Kalshi has also launched FX-related prediction markets, and Ross said “the two of them fit together.”

The statement confirms plans outlined in July, when Chief Risk Officer Udesh Jha said Kalshi was discussing an expansion into FX, metals and energy with regulators. At the time, Jha identified the three categories as those attracting the most investor demand.

Ross rejected the suggestion that adding conventional derivatives means Kalshi is moving away from prediction markets. Instead, he described event contracts and perpetual futures as complementary products that can be offered within the same asset class.

Event contracts allow users to trade a defined outcome, while perpetuals provide continuous directional exposure to an underlying asset.

“We started with these markets in prediction markets for crypto. Then we added delta,” he explained. “We’ve started in prediction markets for metals, and now we’ve added delta.” Kalshi has not disclosed whether it has submitted proposed FX perpetuals for regulatory review.

“They’re There Because Their Clients Are Telling Them”

Asked who is trading on Kalshi’s institutional side, Ross pointed to the scale of the firms entering the market. “We’re seeing people onboard or trading on the market who, if you added them all up together, have got more than a trillion dollars of assets under management,” he said.

Ross also pointed to futures commission merchants connecting to the exchange as evidence of client demand. “They’re not there because it’s really exciting for them,” he said. “They’re there because their clients are telling them, ‘No, no, I need you to do it.’”

“One of the naive things I thought was, the guys who do crypto, they’re going to do crypto, and the guys who do sports are going to do sports, and the guys who do politics are going to do politics because that’s their expertise,” Ross said.

“What I actually found is that because this is an exchange and it’s an order book and the messaging protocols are the same and the data coming out is the same, we actually have people who are interested in sports who also do crypto and also do energy products.”

“We’re seeing people trade on perps as well as prediction markets,” he said, adding that activity also covers weather, financial markets and idiosyncratic risks. Some institutions trade directly, while others use the prices in conventional markets.

Some institutions trade directly, while others use Kalshi prices to inform decisions in conventional markets. Ross described how that can work: “Kalshi could give you a price, and you could look at the Kalshi price and decide what you’re going to do with that on a legacy market.”

As one example, he pointed to nearly $50 million in trading on Kalshi’s market covering the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz. He also recalled a conversation with the head of trading risk at a US oil major:

“The first thing he does in the morning when he wakes up is look at the Strait of Hormuz market, right before he gets out of bed.”

Ross has made the same argument outside the interview, linking the institutional value of prediction markets to continuous price discovery, central clearing and an open order book.

How Kalshi Uses Data to Grow Its Network

Kalshi has also listed markets at the request of individual institutions. Those firms may eventually want enough liquidity to trade the risk, but the immediate value comes from price discovery.

“Day one, there’s value in listing a market and having it priced,” Ross said. The resulting probability can inform decisions involving legislation or political developments that may affect positions in conventional markets.

“Some of it absolutely is a data story,” he added. “We have hundreds of people who have signed up to get data from us. We distribute data via a series of third parties as well.”

For now, wider distribution matters more to Kalshi than data revenue. “Zero per cent of our revenue comes from data monetisation. We charge zero fees for the data,” Ross said. “The more eyeballs you have on the data, the more interesting the market is.”

Kalshi may charge for some data products in the future, but Ross expects its top-of-book probabilities to remain public. “I’m not saying that we will charge zero forever,” he added. “I don’t think there’s any plan ever to remove that sort of top-of-book probabilities from the public domain.”

What Do Kalshi’s Institutional Client Numbers Show?

Ross did not provide a breakdown of institutional participation by type, but offered figures on the number and size of the firms using the exchange.

“What I can say is that we have hundreds of clients that are institutional in size that are trading on Kalshi,” he said. “We’ve got many hundreds of clients that have joined the market across all of those groups that you mentioned before.”

The categories raised in the interview included market makers and end users such as hedge funds, asset managers and corporates.

For brokers weighing whether to build or connect, Ross’s pitch ultimately comes back to the same point: exchange infrastructure can be built or bought, but an existing pool of users, pricing and order-book depth is harder to replicate.

Build or rent? FX and CFD brokers looking to add event contracts face a familiar infrastructure choice: build their own venue or connect to an existing one. For Kalshi’s Head of Institutional Andy Ross, the answer starts with liquidity: “You want to go to the place that’s got all the liquidity.”

The liquidity argument also explains why broker distribution matters to Kalshi: each new connection can bring more participants to the same order book.

London's trading industry is coming home!

Ross said firms onboarding to or already trading on Kalshi collectively manage more than $1 trillion in assets. He described institutional involvement as a ‘significant proportion’ of activity and said institutions frequently trade against other institutions.

The broker channel, however, is only one part of its institutional strategy. The exchange is also adding perpetual futures, including planned FX products, and offering market data to firms that may use its prices without trading the underlying contracts.

Why Building an Exchange Does Not Build Liquidity

Kalshi has begun distributing its event contracts through existing brokerage platforms.

An API-based service launched with Apex Fintech Solutions allows brokers to add the contracts to their own interfaces without creating their own exchange and clearing infrastructure. tastytrade was the first broker to go live.

When asked why a broker should connect rather than build or acquire an exchange, Ross focused on order concentration.

He said that Kalshi’s advantage is the concentration of users “not just through brokers but directly on its platform” and institutional channels, which together are “creating this phenomenal price point.”

Similar event contracts may be available on several venues, but differences in settlement terms and wording can make them non-identical.

“You’ve got to be able to check: is the contract exactly written the same?” Ross said. “But if the products are somewhat analogous and there’s liquidity, then you can go trade on those if you want.”

“You want to go to the place that’s got all the liquidity and all of the pricing and all of the depth in the order book, so that when you put the trade on, you can also get out of the trade,” he added. “It’s important to be able to do that.”

How Brokers Can Add Prediction Markets

The Apex arrangement shows how a broker can give clients access to Kalshi’s order book without operating an exchange itself.

The broker retains its interface and customer relationship, Apex handles clearing, custody, money movement, statements and account management, while Kalshi operates the regulated marketplace and lists the event contracts.

“That client then can use that broker interface and stay in that broker’s ecosystem to be able to get access to prediction markets or get access to the perpetuals that are trading on Kalshi,” Ross said. “The client doesn’t have to go and sign up to seven new places if they want to do that, and so they get a consolidated risk report.”

For the broker, this expands the product range while keeping the customer on its platform. For Kalshi, it brings additional participants and fee-paying order flow.

“We offer an order book, and more people who come to trade on it, we get paid fees for that, obviously,” Ross said. “The quality of the market goes up. Therefore, trading volume goes up.”

He described the arrangement as a “win-win-win” for the customer, broker and exchange.

Why Kalshi Is Expanding Beyond Event Contracts

The products available through Kalshi are also expanding beyond the event contracts on which the exchange built its business.

“People don’t just want prediction markets,” Ross said. “They also want to be able to trade on leveraged delta in perpetuals. And so we’re offering both.”

Kalshi has launched perpetual futures on cryptocurrencies and precious metals, extending the range on 6 October with US500, a contract linked to an index of 500 large US companies.

Unlike traditional options and futures, they don’t expire, so there’s no need to roll over contracts or decide when to exercise an option. Gains and losses are tied directly to how much the market moves, giving you an efficient and straightforward way to ask the question: is the market going up or down? One perpetual contract concentrates liquidity instead of spreading it across expiration dates. Bringing more traders and competing views into a single liquidity pool on a national exchange can strengthen competition, improve pricing, and make markets more efficient over time. This launch brings us closer to building a financial exchange for anyone and everyone. Prediction markets gave traders exposure to the events that move the stock market. The US 500 is the natural next step: a way to trade on the market itself.

title: Mastering the Long Game: An Exclusive Interview with Diego Forlán
summary:
A goal takes a moment. The work that makes it possible takes years. For Diego Forlán, success has always involved decisions made far from the spotlight: how to prepare, when to adapt, and what to do when the result does not reflect the effort.
In this exclusive interview, Forlán looks beyond the big...
content:
A goal takes a moment. The work that makes it possible takes years. For Diego Forlán, success has always involved decisions made far from the spotlight: how to prepare, when to adapt, and what to do when the result does not reflect the effort.

In this exclusive interview, Forlán looks beyond the big occasions to discuss the thinking that sustained his career. He talks about resisting short-term pressure, learning to trust his judgement, and recognising when patience matters more than an immediate impact. His partnership with OneRoyal brings another dimension to the conversation, creating parallels between the demands of football and the uncertainty of trading.

Through it all, he returns to a conviction shaped by experience: one performance should never define the bigger picture.

As a young footballer, what did success look like to you? How did that definition change as your career progressed?

For me, success is having something you believe in and dedicate yourself to. Something you try to do to the best of your abilities. It's not always the result that matters most. It's knowing that, deep down, you committed yourself fully and did everything you could to make things work. Because, sometimes, the result is out of your hands. But the effort, commitment, dedication, and attitude you bring to every challenge are always down to you.

Fans see the goals and the big occasions. What did you do consistently behind the scenes that made those moments possible?

The goals and the special moments are a result of a lot of hard work. It takes dedication, perseverance, and discipline. You need to set your targets and keep moving towards them. To play and succeed at the highest levels, you need to be willing to sacrifice. You need to stick to your plan and that often involves making tough decisions. No matter how well you do, there’s always ways to improve. You need to keep chasing that growth to stay on top of your game.

How did you learn to distinguish between a bad run of form and something in your game that genuinely needed to change?

It’s not always easy. You have to build up an awareness of your own game. Things will never go perfectly 100% of the time, and that’s normal. But, if your performance is constantly falling below the standards you expect, despite putting in the hard work, something may need to change. It often helps to sit down and think about things. Analyse your performances and see if a pattern emerges. If you need to make an adjustment. Or if you’re just in a rut and need to push through.

In a big match, how do you judge when to be patient and when to take a chance?

I think this is something that you develop with experience. When you’re young or just starting out, it can be harder to be patient. You’re excited to make an impact and show what you can do, and that can sometimes override critical thinking. But as you grow, you learn to read the game better. You become more confident in yourself, in your teammates, and in your overall judgement. You start to understand what moves and what opportunities have a higher chance of success, and when it may be better to sit back and wait.

After a great performance, what helped you reset and prepare for the next game? Was that ever harder than responding to a defeat?

Regardless of whether I was coming off a win or a loss, it was always important to take some time to rest and reflect before going again. You should never let one outcome, positive or negative, define what comes next. But there’s always something to learn. Analyse what went well and what you did right, or what you could improve on before the next match. You need to stay focused, remain disciplined, and keep making decisions that lead you closer to your overall goals.

Football demands results immediately, but building a career takes years. How did you keep short-term pressure from affecting your longer-term decisions?

In football, as in life, there are always external and internal pressures. You want to prove yourself, to show you’re capable of succeeding at the highest level. Of making a positive impact for both you and your team. But it’s important not to let these pressures overwhelm you. Giving into them can often have a negative impact on your performance. While difficult, sometimes the best thing to do is just let the pressure bounce off of you. Focus on your long-term goals and aspirations. And keep making decisions every single day that bring you that little bit closer to them. Building a fruitful career is a marathon, not a sprint. Letting short-term pressures influence your decision-making can often take you in the wrong direction.

From what you know of trading, do you see any parallels with football in how people prepare, handle uncertainty, or respond when things don’t go their way?

I think a lot of parallels can be drawn between football and trading. Both are high-pressure environments where split-second decisions can often define success or failure. As in football, trading requires preparation and dedication. You need to work hard, build a plan, and stick to it, even when outside influences may try to push you off track. Whether on the pitch or in the markets, you can never win every time. This is part of the game, but more importantly is how you react to the losses. You can’t let them define you. But you can learn, understand what didn’t work, and improve for the next time. How well you respond to failure often decides how successful you will be in reaching your long-term goals.

Through your relationship with OneRoyal, has anything about the financial world surprised you or sparked your curiosity?

One of the most surprising things to come out of my partnership with OneRoyal is how it has redefined trading for me. I used to think that it was a solo effort. But the truth is that it’s closer to a team sport like football. While a trader is responsible for their own performance, much like a player, when working with a broker like OneRoyal, support is always available. Tools, analysis, and guidance are all provided to help traders make the best decisions in pursuit of their financial goals. Just like the coaches, nutritionists, and equipment footballers have access to. Achievements are also celebrated together. Like with OneRoyal’s upcoming 20th Anniversary Gala in Istanbul, which I’m honoured to be attending, where clients and partners from around the world will gather to celebrate two decades of success.

If you could speak to the young Diego at the very start of his career, what would you tell him?

The first thing I'd tell him is to be patient. To not get too carried away with how things start. The first steps don't always go as you expect. There will always be difficult moments where things don't work out. What's important is to have clear goals that you're always working towards. There's a phrase I've always lived by: in time, everything falls into place. As long as you're working hard, being consistent, patient, and keeping your goal in mind, you'll get there. Don't let singular moments define you. One game, one decision, one thing that didn't go your way. You need to keep your eye on the big picture and understand that achieving your goals is a process.

Forlán’s reflections bring the conversation back to the work that follows the final whistle. There is a performance to assess, something to learn, and another decision to make. His partnership with OneRoyal gives him a new setting in which to explore those ideas, particularly the relationship between personal responsibility and the support around it. The long game, in his telling, is built through the choices made while the outcome is still uncertain.

title: Hyperliquid (HYPE) Price Prediction: Could a Falling Wedge Breakout Send HYPE Above $90?
summary: Hyperliquid (HYPE) is approaching a critical technical zone as traders assess whether its recent correction will extend toward $75 or give way to a recovery above $90.
content:
Skip to content
Assets: HYPE

Hyperliquid (HYPE) is approaching a critical technical zone as traders assess whether its recent correction will extend toward $75 or give way to a recovery above $90.

Several Hyperliquid price analyses identify a potential bullish reversal, but the token still faces resistance that must be cleared before an upward move can be confirmed.

The immediate focus is on the $79.40–$82.50 resistance range, where a breakout could strengthen the recovery outlook. Meanwhile, support around $76.55–$78 and the broader $75 area remains important as HYPE trades below its September peak near $98.

HYPE Price Prediction: Falling Wedge Signals a Potential Reversal

A one-hour chart analysis by TradingView contributor Rendra_Azrulsyah identifies a falling wedge within a descending channel. The pattern reflects a market in which price continues to make lower highs and lower lows, but the distance between the trendlines gradually narrows. A breakout above the upper trendline can signal a potential reversal, although confirmation is necessary.

A confirmed breakout above $82.411 could trigger a bullish reversal, targeting $90.714 or the next swing high. Source: Rendra_Azrulsyah on TradingView

The analysis identifies $75.083 as a potential downside target if selling pressure persists. On the upside, a confirmed move above $82.411 would strengthen the bullish scenario, with the next target near $90.714 at descending-channel resistance.

The $82.411 level is therefore an important threshold for the Hyperliquid price prediction. Until HYPE breaks above that resistance, the falling wedge remains a potential reversal setup rather than evidence that the correction has ended.

Hyperliquid Faces Key Support Near $75

A separate daily-chart analysis places the current correction within a broader rising channel. This suggests that the short-term weakness has not necessarily invalidated the larger upward structure.

HYPEUSD faces downside risk toward $75 and the rising channel’s lower boundary, with a confirmed bullish peak near support needed to signal a potential recovery toward previous highs. Source: Rendra_Azrulsyah on TradingView

The strategy outlined in the analysis calls for a confirmed bullish peak near support before considering a new long position. Such confirmation could indicate that buyers are regaining control after the pullback. A subsequent recovery toward previous highs and the upper boundary of the rising channel would then become a possible scenario.

However, a sustained decline toward $75 or the lower channel boundary would increase the risk of a deeper correction. Traders will need to monitor price reactions around support rather than assume that the broader uptrend guarantees a recovery.

Recent market data reinforces the importance of these levels. CoinGecko’s historical records show that HYPE closed at $94.15 on October 5 before falling to $79.19 on October 19. That decline places the token well below its early-October highs and highlights the selling pressure that bulls must overcome. 

Can HYPE Break Above $80 and Target $98?

TradingView contributor RLinda’s analysis identifies a potential end to Hyperliquid’s countertrend correction, with a recovery dependent on a breakout from the current corrective structure.

The analysis lists $79.40 and $80 as initial resistance levels, followed by $82.50. A sustained move above $80, combined with a breakout above the wedge resistance, could provide an early indication that buying momentum is improving.

A breakout above wedge resistance and the $79.40–$80.00 zone could confirm the end of consolidation and trigger further upside toward the projected targets. Source: RLinda on TradingView

The next upside targets are $88 and $98. The latter would bring HYPE back toward its September peak, according to the supplied market analysis. However, reaching that level would require the token to clear several resistance areas rather than move directly higher.

On the downside, RLinda identifies $76.55 as support. A break below this level could weaken the immediate recovery setup and bring the $75 area back into focus.

The analysis also suggests that a confirmed breakout could trigger short liquidations and encourage new long positions. In leveraged markets, short liquidations occur when traders betting on falling prices are forced to close their positions as prices rise. These forced purchases can accelerate an existing upward move, although the effect depends on market positioning and available liquidity.

Hyperliquid Liquidity Heatmap Highlights $78 and $85

Liquidity levels are another factor shaping the near-term HYPE price prediction. Trader MookieNFT highlighted potential liquidation clusters around $78 below the market and $85 above it using a Coinglass liquidation heatmap.

The HYPE liquidation heatmap highlights major liquidity clusters at $85 above and $78 below, leaving the next price move dependent on which level gets tested first. Source: @MookieNFT via X

These zones matter because leveraged positions can become vulnerable when prices approach areas containing concentrated liquidation levels. A move toward $78 could put some leveraged long positions under pressure, while a rally toward $85 could challenge short positions.

hello, world.

— XRP (@XRP) October 19, 2026

According to the profile, XRP is a decentralized, payments-focused blockchain with a native token. It also mentions that the account is shared by both Ripple and the XRP Ledger Foundation.

The organization of that structure will provide a direct connection with two of the most prominent organizations in the XRP ecosystem and will focus on XRP and not one organization.

Right after that account appeared, Ripple jumped the bandwagon and embraced the launch. CFO Brad Garlinghouse also spoke out on social media, hinting that it had been expected for quite a while.

Updates have been around the corner for XRP previously, but from Ripple, the developers of the XRP Ledger, community, and XRP ecosystem organizations. Communication via the official @XRP account will be easier to discern and keep track of when it is in a standalone existence.

Ripple and XRPL Foundation Share Management

Ripple and the XRP Ledger Foundation will run the account together, the profile reads.

Whoever it might be, be it a company or a native asset of a blockchain, this distinction makes Ripple valuable since it employs products and services developed with XRP and XRPL technology, while XRP is the asset of the blockchain. Also, there is a disclaimer on the account informing the users that it does not provide investment advice.

A detailed publishing plan has not been announced. It is not yet known if the account will feature updates to XRP Ledger, ecosystem projects, payments development and community activity or any other XRP-related announcements.

For XRP, the new account provides a new layer of identity for the blockchain asset, at a time when communication across crypto ecosystems is gaining importance.

title: Cysic Bridge Exploit Mints 10M CYS, Leaves 2.8M Tokens Frozen on BNB Chain
summary:
Key Takeaways: An attacker managed to create 10 million CYS using the Cysic cross-chain bridge on BNB Smart Chain. Cysic blacklisted the recipient address, thereby freezing approximately 2.8 million CYS
The post Cysic Bridge Exploit Mints 10M CYS, Leaves 2.8M Tokens Frozen on BNB Chain appeared firs...
content:
Key Takeaways:

  • An attacker managed to create 10 million CYS using the Cysic cross-chain bridge on BNB Smart Chain.
  • Cysic blacklisted the recipient address, thereby freezing approximately 2.8 million CYS still in the add.
  • No assets on the mainnet were affected by the incident nor were any existing assets impacted.

The cross-chain bridge was suspended by the Cryptic Foundation due to an exploit in the Cross Chain Bridging message processing and minting flow that allowed an attacker to create 10 million CYS without authorization.

https://t.co/bK2X8Ca2sk

— Cysic Foundation (@cysic_fdn) October 18, 2026

The team indicated that such a breach was limited to the bridge infrastructure and not to the consensus mechanism (Cysic mainnet), execution of transactions, or existing tokens in user wallets.

  • Cysic Bridge Mints 10 Million CYS Without Authorization
  • 2.8 Million CYS Remain Restricted
    • Mainnet and Existing User Assets Were Not Hit
    • Cross-Chain Bridge Stays Closed During Review

Cysic Bridge Mints 10 Million CYS Without Authorization

The mint was unauthorized at 12:31:38 UTC 2026/10/17 on BNB Smart Chain.An unauthorized mint happened at 17:31:38 UTC 2026/10/17 on BNB Smart Chain.

In the preliminary investigation, Syschick decided the attacker had successfully breached access to a database that service supporting the bridge was using, and then exploited a vulnerability in the related processing logic to send a fraudulent mint message.

That message resulted in the creation of 10 million CYS at a single recipient address. Cysic urged against considering the count of the token as the bottom line. Actual dollar affect and transfers and swaps are still under investigation.

Read More: Liquid Network Pauses After 4,000 BTC Worth $320M Pulled in White-Hat Incident

2.8 Million CYS Remain Restricted

Cysic began adding the receiver address to the CYS token contract blacklist at 13:47:52 UTC, about 76 minutes after the illicit money printing.

The restriction was activated onchain, and is currently hindering transfers for approximately 2.8 million CYS still held at the address. The team is still tracking down the next $3,380.41, using help from a professional security firm.

Mainnet and Existing User Assets Were Not Hit

The dispute was not to challenge the bridge’s message-processing and minting capabilities, Cysic said.

Its mainnet hasn’t been affected by the infrastructure as yet, and all consensus, block-production and transaction-confirmation and EVM-execution features remain unaffected.

There was also no evidence of any existing CYS or other assets being stolen from user wallets, the foundation added. That is significant because the exploit was not a depleter but did, instead, create new tokens that users were not holding.

Read More: CoinEx Announces Permanent Shutdown After 9 Years, Withdrawals End Dec. 22

Cross-Chain Bridge Stays Closed During Review

Cysic immediately suspended the operation of the bridges after the incident was detected and stated the service will not be reinstated until the whole work flow is reviewed. The investigation now extends to the handling of the messages, the permissions settings, the asset records and the entire attack path.

Cysic has yet to announce a reopening date. The bridge will not reopen until the security assessment is finished and the remediation recommended will be verified.

When in the investigation phase there will be a follow-up report to include the benefits of the investigation and with actual losses derived; progress of fund-tracing and the final remediation steps will be included.

  • 87.1% of the dollars withdrawn are still on-chain, with MEXC holding the remaining 12.9% in its system.

Qubic has suspended its network after an attacker exploited weak wallet seeds and drained thousands of accounts in a security incident spanning October 17 – 18. The insufficiency of randomness was the issue of not the Qubic protocol itself, the project said.

Security incident update.

Between 23:42 UTC on 17 October and 01:26 UTC on 18 October, an attacker drained 1,404 Qubic wallets, totalling around 2.94 trillion QU.

Here is what happened, what has been done, and what comes next. https://t.co/7aPJ26lEeZ

— Qubic (@_Qubic_) October 18, 2026

  • Qubic Freezes Network After 1,404 Wallets Are Drained
  • Version 4.26.4 Fixes the Seed Generation Issue
    • Recovery Process Moves to the Computor Quorum

Qubic Freezes Network After 1,404 Wallets Are Drained

The attack was carried out between Oct. 17, 00:42 UTC and Oct. 18, 01:26 UTC and impacted about 1,404 wallets, eradicating approximately 2.94 trillion QU. Transaction processing was halted by Computors, which have established a protective network halt at tick 85,371,949, the time at which the incident was said to occur.

That action has hindered the attacker’s ability to freely move the stolen wealth. Qubic said that 87.1% of the deleted QU never went out of the net and are stuck there. The remainder (12.9%) went to crypto exchange MEXC, which froze the receiving wallet approximately one hour after receiving a call.

Notifying and suspending QUBIC deposits and withdrawals was also done for other exchanges.

Qubic is tracing the incident back to the lack of randomness in wallet seeds. The impacted app versions are: all generated seeds before October 18, 2026, in Safari on Mac before the same date, and the Qubic iOS app up to July 2025.

Read More: Bitget Halts Withdrawals After $351.6M Hot Wallet Incident Hits Crypto Exchange

Version 4.26.4 Fixes the Seed Generation Issue

The problem has already been addressed for version 4.26.4, so no weak seeds will be formed with it, said the project.

The Core team has now started to find all the impacted wallets and is ready to take the necessary steps to recover them. The quorum of the Computor shall take the final decision on the frozen funds, in accordance with the governance rules of Qubic’s network.

They’re also holding a community poll over Discord, to better understand the sentiment of Computors before they put in a proposal for recovery.

Recovery Process Moves to the Computor Quorum

Normal transaction processing has not been announced by Qubic yet. Affected users have been urged to police or cybercrime authorities and provide their wallet ID, amount lost and relevant links within the Qubic explorer of the transaction.

It could be helpful to involve exchanges in maintaining freezes on associated funds in the form of a formal report. Qubic also cautioned against recovery scams saying its team would never reach out to customers initially to ask them for wallet seeds or provide paid recovery services.

Once the network comes to a decision about the recovery and frozen QU’s, a full technical report should be expected.

content:
Key Takeaways:

  • Bitcoin bull Michael Saylor suggested that Strategy will be buying another Bitcoin.
  • Currently, Strategy has 848,250 BTC owned, worth approximately $69.45 billion.
  • The average price on the Bitcoin that it purchased is $75,444; and the reserve has gained 8.15%.

It’s no surprise that Michael Saylor has reignited rumours regarding a possible Strategy Bitcoin buy after posting, “We found room for more orange” and an updated chart detailing the company’s accumulation history.

We found room for more orange. https://t.co/XAgiEZbXgO

— Michael Saylor (@saylor) October 18, 2026

At the time of this article, Strategy has 848,250 BTC in its possession, confirming its status as one of the biggest corporate Bitcoin holders at the moment.

  • Strategy’s Bitcoin Reserve Reaches $69.45 Billion
  • “More Orange” Signals Another Possible Purchase
    • 848,250 BTC Equals More Than 4% of Bitcoin’s Maximum Supply
    • Strategy Shows No Sign of Ending Its Bitcoin Accumulation

Strategy’s Bitcoin Reserve Reaches $69.45 Billion

The current Saylor’s chart pegs Strategy’s stash at about $69,450,000,000 worth of Bitcoin. The company’s distribution price averaged $75,444 per BTC, and the portfolio held a $5.23 billion or 8.15% unrealized profit at the time of the snapshot.

It also shows 118 Bitcoin acquisition deals that Strategy has gone into, showing the building of its holdings over multiple market cycles instead of a single massive buy.

That’s consistent even though Bitcoin has dipped below its average purchase price as well as surged above $100,000.

Read More: Strategy Restarts Bitcoin Buying with $370M Purchase after 10-Week Pause

“More Orange” Signals Another Possible Purchase

Saylor’s message didn’t reveal the amount or cost of the new purchase or the date of the purchase.

“We found room for more orange” was written, however, with the same Bitcoin buying chart from Strategy, which has orange to mark different previous purchases.

However, the post does not say that it is for the next one to be added as it has not been added yet. As of Saylor’s latest chart, 848,250 BTC is still counted as the confirmed balance as there is no official purchase disclosure yet from Strategy.

848,250 BTC Equals More Than 4% of Bitcoin’s Maximum Supply

As of now, Strategy owns about 4.04% of the 21 million Bitcoin that will ever be in existence. Each new sale of Strategy is scrutinised by crypto markets, especially since the Bitcoin supply is finite and production is gradually slowing.

The total acquisition cost of Strategy’s Bitcoin holdings is about $64 billion, at an average price of $75,444. On October 18, the value of the company’s ground-topping Bitcoin holdings stood at $69.45 billion which put the firm in a strong position, despite the price of Bitcoin trading being relatively low on the day.

Strategy Shows No Sign of Ending Its Bitcoin Accumulation

What Saylor is asserting in his latest post is a business strategy the company has been undertaking, and it’s of handling Bitcoin as a main treasury reserve asset. The chart clearly signals that the price of Bitcoins has been a trend of accumulation throughout different bull and bear markets since Strategy’s initial purchase in 2020.

As for now, the new message isn’t confirmation of fresh buying, but rather a signal. Whether or not Saylor’s “more orange” comment came before he added a newly increased, and large, 848,250 BTC holding to the current total of 663,515 BTC will be recorded in the next official disclosure.

  • 🎭 Entertainment & Community

In 2025 the state government passed a Strategic Arizona Bitcoin Reserve, but I understand the state still hasn’t bought any coins. We can’t wait for the government to use bitcoin before we use it, or it will never happen.

The question is, can a normal person walk into a shop and pay with bitcoin? I have some friends in Scottsdale who have never used bitcoin in real life, so I asked them to test it. I recommended downloading a lightning wallet, sent them some satoshis, and sent them the BTC Map. They were surprised how easy it was to download a wallet and move satoshis across the internet; it felt very natural and how money should be, they said.

First Stop: Pita Cafe (23535 N Scottsdale Rd #102, Scottsdale, AZ 85255)

Their first stop was Pita Cafe, a Mediterranean spot attached to Scottsdale Burger Bar. Both accept bitcoin. My friends came back raving about the food: everything is made fresh to order, and they say to get the spanakopita and the gyro pita. The place was packed at lunch, but service stayed fast with plenty of seating.

The cashier wasn’t sure at first whether they took bitcoin. Then he noticed the Square terminal was already set up for it, and the payment went through quickly. It was his first time seeing customers pay in bitcoin, and he was excited about it. My friends also told me he looked at the amount on the screen and said he was shocked that they’d just paid “22,000 bitcoin”. They walked out feeling like royalty.

Next Up Echo Coffee (2902 N 68th Street, Ste. 135 Scottsdale, Arizona 85251)

Next they got hot cocoa at Echo Coffee. This cashier didn’t need to figure anything out. She knew they accepted bitcoin, switched the terminal over, and asked my friend to scan the QR code. She told them she thinks it’s super cool every time someone asks about it. Echo also donates 1% of purchases to the humane society, and the coffee bags have puppies on them. 

Why this matters

It’s a blast to send your loved ones out to a store along with some bitcoin to spend. Some friends already have bitcoin in investment portfolios, but the act of spending btc for tangible items shows what this movement is all about.

title: World ID Targets $40B AI Fraud Threat With Proofs for Banks, Zoom and AI Agents
summary:
Key Takeaways: World introduced World ID for Banking & Financial Services to fight against AI impersonation. The suite includes features for customer identity, Zoom calls and AI agents with cryptographic
The post World ID Targets $40B AI Fraud Threat With Proofs for Banks, Zoom and AI Agents appeare...
content:
Key Takeaways:

  • World introduced World ID for Banking & Financial Services to fight against AI impersonation.
  • The suite includes features for customer identity, Zoom calls and AI agents with cryptographic Proofs.
  • Initial design partners are Bain Capital, OpenExchange, Outtake, Pantera Capital Funds and VanEck Funds.

World is embedding its Proof of Human technology into banking and finance, as deepfakes and AI impersonation increases risk in banking and finance processes, such as approving transactions, sensitive communication and more.

The new suite is designed to help institutions verify that a real, authorized human is behind a request without relying solely on traditional identity checks.

In 2024, an employee at engineering firm Arup transferred $25.6 million after joining a video call where every other participant was a deepfake. Since then, AI has advanced significantly and is making impersonation increasingly convincing, causing challenges for financial institutions in particular. As autonomous agents begin handling more financial activity on behalf of people, establishing an added layer of trust and security behind a transaction or sensitive conversation is becoming an urgent need.

Introducing @world_id for banking and finance, a suite of technologies that helps institutions establish trust through privacy-preserving cryptographic Proofs. World ID for Zoom lets meeting participants confirm they are the same Orb-verified human connected to their account, while World ID for agents allows AI agents to carry Proofs delegated by people. Bain Capital, OpenExchange, Outtake, Pantera Capital, and VanEck Funds are initial design partners, bringing World ID into some of finance’s most consequential interactions.

— World (@worldnetwork) October 19, 2026

  • World ID Brings Privacy-Preserving Proofs Into Finance
  • World ID for Zoom Verifies the Human Behind the Call
    • AI Agents Can Carry Proofs From Real People
    • Major Finance Firms Join as Design Partners

World ID Brings Privacy-Preserving Proofs Into Finance

With World ID for banking and finance, cryptographic proofs can be used to enable institutions to verify a certain claim about a person without disclosing everything about them.

The system has been designed to provide extra confidence when accessing accounts, authorizing financial transactions, engaging in private discussions and transactions with sensitive material.

World focused on the global rise of the issue of AI impersonation, citing the case of an Arup employee who transferred $25.6 million into an account after being drawn into a conference call where everyone else on the call was a deep fake.

Since then, there have been more advancements in AI-generated voices and facial images, along with in the creation of autonomous agents, which has put the pressure on financial companies to differentiate between impossible to false identities.

Read More: Vitalik Warns AI Math Could Threaten Crypto Keys Before Quantum Computing Arrives

World ID for Zoom Verifies the Human Behind the Call

World ID is also provided for Zoom confirming the person being addressed, or the user verified as being a human by using Orb.

The point is that it is not just about being able to identify if a face is fake, it is about giving the moniker “cryptographic proof” that the person in a sensitive meeting is connected to a previous verified identity of a human being.

This might come in handy with high-value financial approvals or communications with executives/accounts being recovered that could result in substantial losses if a deepfake succeeded.

AI Agents Can Carry Proofs From Real People

World is also working on extending identity verification to AI agents. World ID for Agents enables a person to pass over selected Proofs to an AI system, indicating that it’s delegating on his or her behalf.

This provides an anticipatory ID system for semi-autonomous software to more contingent perform transactions, purchases, etc. It does not require the institution to trust a bot that they have never dealt with before, but provides the agent with a verifiable link back to a human user without compromising privacy.

Read More: Robinhood Launches AI-Native Chain, Stock Tokens in 120+ Countries and 7% Crypto Yield

Major Finance Firms Join as Design Partners

World has stated it is working with Bain Capital, OpenExchange, Outtake, Pantera Capital and VanEck Funds as early design partners. The launch comes as AI-related fraud is becoming a larger financial risk. Deloitte estimates losses from generative AI-powered fraud will amount to $12.3 billion in 2023 and quadruple to $40 billion by 2027.

Word is making its Proof-based identity infrastructure about giving financial institutions trust without requiring consumers to give more personal information than is needed.

Zug, Switzerland, October 19th, 2026, Chainwire

StakerX’s AI Agent Surpasses Passes $40M Staked Assets on Solana Within Three Months of Launch

StakerGPT trades crypto markets around the clock and publishes every trade it makes, as more than 8,200 users join the platform

StakerX.ai, an agentic trading platform built by Switzerland-based StakerX Strategies AG, has passed $40 million in assets staked on Solana less than three months after its public launch on July 13, 2026. Users fund their stakes with more than 40 cryptocurrencies from most major blockchains, and StakerGPT, the platform’s agentic trading agent, puts that capital to work in crypto perpetual futures markets every day.

An AI agent that shows its work

An agentic system is AI software that carries out a multi-step task on its own. StakerGPT is built on rare-access Claude Mythos: it monitors crypto markets around the clock, reasons over potential trade setups, filters them through risk controls and routes the approved trades for execution, without a human placing each order.

Every trade is public. StakerX publishes the full record daily at stakerx.ai/trades, with the market, direction, entry and exit prices and return of each position, including both live-executed and signal-derived trades. As of October 18, 2026, the record holds 804 trades across 139 trading days since June 1, 2026, so anyone can check what the agent did on any given day instead of relying on summary figures.

Fund it with almost any coin

Users can deposit USDC, USDT, BTC, ETH, SOL, BNB, TRX and more than 30 other cryptocurrencies from Solana, Ethereum, Bitcoin, BNB Chain, Base, Arbitrum, Polygon, Tron and other networks. Each deposit is converted and credited as USDC, a dollar-backed stablecoin, on Solana, so users do not need to bridge or swap anything themselves. Stakes start at $10 and run for 30 days.

Three months of growth

As of October 18, 2026, StakerX.ai reports:

  • $40 million currently staked on the platform
  • More than 8,200 registered users, of whom more than 3,000 have funded an account
  • 804 trades published across 139 trading days
  • More than 27,700 completed withdrawals, totalling $10+ million
  • Nearly $12 million in yield credited to users since launch

Coming to the App Store and Google Play

StakerX is preparing native mobile apps for iOS and Android, expected in December 2026, which will bring the dashboard, deposits and the live StakerGPT trade record to the Apple App Store and Google Play. The platform is available today on the web at stakerx.ai.

About StakerX

StakerX is an agentic trading platform built and operated by StakerX Strategies AG, a quantitative trading and investment firm based in Switzerland. Its AI trading agent, StakerGPT, is built on rare-access Claude Mythos and evaluates crypto markets, applies risk filters and routes trades, and the platform publishes every trade in its record daily. Its goal is to make agentic trading accessible to anyone who holds crypto, from any chain, with every trade on the record. StakerX launched publicly on July 13, 2026. More information is available at stakerx.ai.
